description:
The City is implementing improvements to Master Lift Station No. 11 that will impact the existing asphalt parking lot at Manor Lanes along NE 26th Drive. As part of the project, the City will restore and reconfigure portions of the parking lot affected by the lift station improvements.
The proposed parking lot work includes milling and resurfacing or overlay of the existing asphalt parking lot, reconstruction of access drive aisles from NE 26th Drive, reconfiguration of parking spaces, installation of new pavement markings, and removal and reinstallation of existing wheel stops and signage.
Chen Moore and Associates, the City's engineering consultant under RFQ 2020-09, has submitted a proposal to provide professional engineering services for the parking lot improvements. The scope includes preparation of design plans, technical specifications and cost estimates; geotechnical investigation; bidding assistance; construction document review; and construction observation services.
CMA's proposed fee is $35,435.00, consisting of $27,050.00 for design services and $8,385.00 for construction services. Approval of the Purchase Order will allow the parking lot restoration design to proceed in coordination with the Master Lift Station No. 11 improvements.

Seventh Amendment to CGA for NW 3rd Ave Drainage_signed

description:
The NW 3rd Avenue Drainage Improvements Project (Project) consists of the replacement and enhancement of the City’s existing stormwater drainage system along NW 3rd Avenue between NW 23rd Street and NW 20th Street, including portions of NW 21st Court and the existing outfall to the South Fork of Middle River. The improvements include replacement and upsizing of stormwater piping and drainage structures, construction of an exfiltration trench and outfall improvements, installation of grass swales, and related restoration.
On November 28, 2023, the City Commission authorized Calvin, Giordano & Associates, Inc (CGA) to design and prepare construction documents for the Project. On July 28, 2026, the City Commission approved the award of the construction contract for the Project to Kailas Corp in the amount of $844,912.00. The project is funded through the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency Water Infrastructure Finance and Innovation Act (WIFIA) loan program.
CGA has submitted a proposal to provide professional engineering services during the estimated nine-month construction period. The proposed scope includes updating the final bid documents to incorporate federal funding requirements; conducting the pre-construction meeting and construction progress meetings; reviewing shop drawings, submittals, requests for information, payment applications, and proposed changes; providing interpretation and clarification of the contract documents; reviewing as-built documentation; assisting with permit certification and project closeout; and performing substantial and final completion inspections.
The scope also includes part-time Resident Project Representative services throughout construction. These services include construction observation for compliance with the plans and specifications, weekly observation reports, coordination with the contractor, identification of deficient or non-conforming work, observation of drainage testing, review of NPDES practices, and assistance with project closeout.
CGA’s proposed fee is $58,768.14, consisting of $889.55 for document updates for recent utility fiber installations in the project area, $17,073.06 for professional engineering services during construction, $35,805.53 for Resident Project Representative services, and a $5,000.00 allowance for additional engineering tasks. The additional engineering allowance will only be utilized upon written direction from the City.

description:
The proposed Code Enforcement Lien Settlement Agreement between the City of Wilton Manors and Wilton West, LLC addresses outstanding liens associated with three properties: 409 NW 25 Street, 925 NW 30 Court, and 1009 NW 30 Court. The properties were brought into compliance in 2023; however, fines accrued before compliance resulted in liens totaling $191,400. Wilton West previously paid $17,328, leaving an outstanding balance of $174,072.
The City Commission considered compromising these liens on July 8, 2025, and again on October 13, 2026. The proposed agreement establishes a total settlement amount of $143,550, less the $17,328 previously paid, resulting in a remaining principal balance of $126,222. The agreement recognizes Wilton West’s expenditures for installation of a stormwater drainage system at the 409 NW 25 Street property and the public interest in resolving the outstanding liens without litigation.
Under the proposed terms, Wilton West must pay $13,890.17 in accrued interest upon execution of the agreement, followed by 18 monthly payments of $7,457.32, including interest, beginning November 10, 2026, and ending April 10, 2028. Payments must be made by ACH transfer. Sale of any of the properties accelerates payment of the entire outstanding compromised balance.
The agreement includes a five-day grace period for payments and requires continued code compliance at all three properties. Failure to meet the payment requirements, or failure to timely correct a future code violation resulting in a Special Magistrate finding, makes the original lien amounts immediately due, with payments credited as provided in the agreement. The agreement also provides for reinstatement of the original lien amounts, less payments, if the City is joined in a foreclosure proceeding involving any of the properties.
Wilton West acknowledges the validity of the liens and waives related claims and defenses. The agreement will be recorded in Broward County’s public records at Wilton West’s expense and will bind successors and assigns. Upon completion of the required payments, the City must record releases of the liens within ten days.

The City's switch network infrastructure currently relies on a mix of switch types and manufacturers, many of which have reached or are approaching the end of their manufacturer-supported life cycle.
To address this, staff is standardizing the network switch platform across the enterprise (all sites) while implementing centralized management, replacing the current legacy equipment. This consolidates the switch network onto a single, supported product family and enables visibility across the entire network from a single management portal. Centralized management improves system monitoring and simplifies software/firmware upgrades, helping ensure systems remain secure and current.

Fiscal Impact Analysis Proposed Amendments to Comp Plan 2nd reading 10.27.26

description:
Amendments are proposed to the City of Wilton Manors Comprehensive Plan related to the Evaluation and Appraisal Review ("EAR") that is required by Florida Statute 163.3191. The purpose of the EAR is to evaluate the City’s Comprehensive Plan to determine if any plan amendments are necessary to reflect the minimum planning period of at least 10 years, to reflect changes in state requirements, and any updates to the plan based on changes to local conditions. These changes include, but are not limited to updates to dates, housing demographics, population projections, agency and department names, updates to be consistent with Broward County’s Comprehensive Plan, state mandated addition of a Property Rights Element in accordance with Florida Statute 163.3177(6)(i), and state mandated updates to reflect City of Wilton Manor’s 20-Year Water Supply Facilities Plan as required by Florida Statutes 163.3177(6)(c)3 and 373.709. These proposed amendments to the City’s Comprehensive Plan will not have any impact on the City’s level of service standards. The table attached includes a summary of the proposed changes to the City’s Comprehensive Plan. Approval of the proposed amendments to the City's Comprehensive Plan is subject to final review and approval of the City Attorney.
The First Reading of the Evaluation and Appraisal Review (EAR) related to amendments to the City’s Comprehensive Plan, the addition of a Property Rights Element, and the updated 2020 Water Supply Plan was on May 26, 2026. A motion was made by Commissioner Bracchi and seconded by Vice Mayor Caputo to approve Ordinance 2026-011. Motion passed with a 5-0 vote.
After First Reading by the City Commission, the proposed amendments to the City's Comprehensive Plan were transmitted to the Florida Department of Commerce for review on June 8, 2026 and distributed to other applicable state agencies, Broward County, the South Florida Regional Planning Council, the Broward County School Board, and adjacent cities. Based on suggested comments made by the State, minor changes were made to dates throughout the plan. The changes are shown in the text of the comprehensive plan are highlighted in blue and yellow. Blue highlight references changes seen by the State and yellow highlight references additional changes made after the State's subsequent review. In addition, language was added to the body of the ordinance authorizing the transmittal of the state adopted amendments to the Broward County Planning Council for the recertification of the Future Land Use Element after the adopted EAR based on amendments are transmitted to the state.
title: Ordinance No. 2026-011: (Community Development Services) (Second Reading) AN ORDINANCE OF THE CITY COMMISSION OF THE CITY OF WILTON MANORS, FLORIDA, AMENDING THE CITY OF WILTON MANORS COMPREHENSIVE PLAN, ADOPTING THE EVALUATION AND APPRAISAL REVIEW (“EAR”) BASED AMENDMENTS TO THE CITY’S COMPREHENSIVE PLAN, ADDING A PROPERTY RIGHTS ELEMENT, AND UPDATING THE 20 YEAR WATER SUPPLY FACILITIES PLAN, A COPY OF WHICH IS ATTACHED AS EXHIBIT “A”; PROVIDING FOR TRANSMITTAL; PROVIDING FOR CONFLICTS; PROVIDING FOR SEVERABILITY; AND PROVIDING FOR AN EFFECTIVE DATE.

attachments.name: Memorandum to Fill Full-Time IT System's Administrator

description:
Staff is requesting authorization to fill a vacant full-time IT System's Administrator position within the Information Technology Department, as well as authorization to backfill any vacancy resulting from the internal promotion of an existing employee into this position. The position became vacant on October 6, 2026, and is responsible for providing essential technical support across all City departments, including maintaining computer systems, network equipment, Microsoft 365 accounts, telecommunications, software applications, and cybersecurity systems.
The IT System's Administrator serves as a primary point of contact for technical support requests and plays a critical role in maintaining the City's technology infrastructure and supporting daily operations, including those of the Police Department and other public safety personnel. Staff advises that failure to fill this vacancy would result in increased helpdesk response times, delays in resolving technical issues, reduced support for employee onboarding and separation processes, and additional workload for remaining IT personnel. These challenges could also impact routine system maintenance, cybersecurity oversight, and overall operational efficiency.
The position is already funded within the City's approved budget. Filling the vacancy, along with any resulting vacancy from an internal promotion, will help ensure continuity of essential technology services, maintain cybersecurity and licensing compliance, and preserve the level of technical support required for effective City operations.
title: Request to Fill Full-Time IT System's Administrator Vacancy

MMOA_IN ROAD SOLAR LIGHTING_CITY OF WILTON MANORS_2026-C-491-00003_FINAL 09-28-26

description:
The City is proceeding with the Powerline Road Crosswalk Lighting Project along State Road 845 (NW 9th Avenue/Powerline Road) near NW 25th Street. The project includes installation of a solar-powered in-road midblock crosswalk warning lighting system within FDOT right-of-way under Permit No. 2026-C-491-00003.Because the improvements will be constructed within State Road 845 right-of-way, FDOT requires the City to enter into a Maintenance Memorandum of Agreement establishing the responsibilities of the City and FDOT for the improvements.
Under the MMOA, the City will be responsible for construction and ongoing maintenance of the solar-powered crosswalk warning system, including the associated in-road lighting, batteries, electrical components, control cabinets, poles, solar panels, and related equipment. The City will also be responsible for inspection, repair, restoration, replacement, and general maintenance of the improvements in accordance with applicable FDOT standards and requirements.
The agreement requires the City to maintain the improvements in a fully operational condition and to address defective or damaged components resulting from normal wear, accidents, vandalism, weather events, or other causes. The City is also required to coordinate work affecting traffic with FDOT and maintain appropriate traffic control and pedestrian access during maintenance activities.
The MMOA will remain in effect for as long as the improvements remain within the FDOT right-of-way. Approval of the resolution will authorize the City to enter into the required agreement with FDOT and allow the Powerline Road Crosswalk Lighting Project to proceed in accordance with the FDOT permit.

attachments.name: 2026-086 RESO Approving Eighth Amendment Chen Moore and Associates, Inc. (2020-09)
8th  amendment to ChenMoore-City of Wilton Manors Continuing Services Agreement signed 10012026

description:
The City of Wilton Manors has been awarded a Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA) Hazard Mitigation Grant Program (HMGP) award, administered by the Florida Division of Emergency Management (FDEM), to prepare a Citywide Watershed Master Plan. The grant provides $150,000 in federal funding toward a total project cost of $200,000. The required $50,000 non-federal match will be satisfied through documented in-kind City staff services.
The proposed amendment and associated work authorization will add the grant-funded Watershed Master Plan scope to the City's existing agreement with Chen Moore and Associates, Inc. Chen Moore will serve as the prime consultant and retain Brizaga as a subconsultant. The consultant team will use and build upon the analyses and work products Chen Moore and Brizaga prepared while developing the City's Joint Adaptation Plan, reducing duplication and maintaining consistency among the City's resilience planning documents. The consultant team will complete the work for a lump-sum fee of $150,000, consistent with the federal share included in the approved grant budget. Invoices will be submitted monthly based on the percentage of each task completed.
The scope follows the nine tasks established in the City's approved grant sub-application. Major elements include data collection and watershed characterization; hydrologic and hydraulic modeling of the 10-, 25-, and 100-year storm events under current and future sea level rise and climate conditions; identification of critical assets and flood-prone areas; regulatory review; evaluation of traditional and nature-based improvements; draft and final plan preparation; Community Rating System (CRS), National Flood Insurance Program (NFIP), and Broward County Local Mitigation Strategy coordination; City Commission adoption; and required reporting to FDEM.
The consultant team proposes to complete the Watershed Master Plan within 18 months, from September 1, 2026, through March 1, 2028. This schedule is within the grant's performance period of March 11, 2026, through May 31, 2028. The completed plan will guide future stormwater capital improvements, strengthen the City's competitiveness for outside funding, support the City's goal of rejoining the Community Rating System, and improve long-term flood resilience.

description:
Article 030 of the City’s Unified Land Development Regulations (ULDRs) includes the City of Wilton Manors’ definitions, regulations, and development requirements for the City’s Urban Center Mixed-Use Districts which are defined as the Wilton Drive Arts and Entertainment District (WDAE), Transit-Oriented Corridor North District (TOC-N), Transit-Oriented Corridor South District (TOC-S), Transit-Oriented Corridor East District (TOC-E), and Transit-Oriented Corridor West District (TOC-W). The purpose of the Urban Center Mixed-Use Districts is to encourage and facilitate the development of a mixture of residential units, entertainment, cultural facilities, restaurants, shopping, commercial, retail, and professional office uses. The City Commission has directed city staff to amend Article 030 to reflect Commission priorities as well as to incorporate feedback received from the community and developers. The proposed amendments include, but are not limited to, changes to alcohol distance separation requirements for establishments, definitions, permitted and prohibited uses, absolute maximum height, building design provisions, off-street parking requirements, and signage requirements.
This item was tabled from the August 25, 2026 City Commission meeting by the City Commission. First reading of the agenda item was held on September 8, 2026. Due to changes made at the September 8, 2026 City Commission meeting, the City Attorney requested an additional First Reading of the proposed changes to Article 030 of the City's ULDRs.
The following changes have been made since First Reading by the City Commission on September 8, 2026.The elimination of the proposed height changes.
A revision to multifamily parking requirements to require 1.25 parking spaces for freestanding multifamily and 1.15 parking spaces for multifamily that is part of a mixed-use building.
The following changes have been made since the second First Reading on September 22, 2026:
The use listed in Section 030-030 - Detailed table of permitted and prohibited uses as proposed, was changed from "Dwelling, multi-family,(within a mixed-use building)" to "Dwelling, multi-family and or townhouses, (within a mixed-use project).

description:
The Wilton Manors Police Department has been approved to participate in the Alert Today Florida High Visibility Enforcement (HVE) Pedestrian and Bicycle Safety Program, administered through the Institute of Police Technology and Management (IPTM) in coordination with the Florida Department of Transportation (FDOT). The program supports targeted education and enforcement efforts aimed at reducing pedestrian and bicycle crashes by increasing awareness and compliance with traffic laws.
Under the agreement, the City is eligible to receive up to $5,000 in reimbursable funding for eligible overtime and associated costs incurred by Wilton Manors Police Department personnel while conducting approved HVE activities.
The agreement also contains indemnification provisions requiring the City, to the extent permitted by law, to indemnify and hold harmless IPTM and the State of Florida/FDOT from certain claims arising from the City's negligence, recklessness, or intentional wrongful conduct. attachments.name: 2026-070 Approving JPA with Broward County for Andrews Ave Corridor Project

description:
The attached Joint Participation Agreement (JPA) between Broward County and the City of Wilton Manors establishes the responsibilities of each party for the relocation, adjustment, and replacement of approximately 5,400 linear feet of City water mains located within the Andrews Avenue Corridor Project from the South Fork of the Middle River to Oakland Park Boulevard. Broward County is undertaking roadway, drainage, pedestrian, lighting, and signal improvements along Andrews Avenue and has agreed to incorporate the City's water main replacement into the County's construction contract to provide a coordinated, cost-effective project delivery. Replacement of the Andrews Avenue 8” watermain is identified as a project in the Water, Wastewater, and Stormwater Integrated Master Plan.
Under the Agreement, Broward County will manage the design, permitting, bidding, construction, and construction engineering and inspection (CEI) services for the utility improvements as part of the overall roadway project. The City will participate in the review and approval of the design plans, specifications, and cost estimate prior to advertisement for construction.
The City's financial participation is capped at $3,000,000, subject to adjustments for unforeseen conditions or bid amounts exceeding the approved estimate. The City will provide an initial payment of $300,000 for design services within 30 days of the Agreement's effective date and the remaining $2,700,000 for construction and CEI after approval of the final plans and cost estimate. Any unused funds will be returned to the City following project completion, while any additional costs resulting from unforeseen conditions or approved change orders remain the City's responsibility.
The Agreement also requires the City to waive applicable City permit and inspection fees, assist with obtaining permits from other agencies when necessary, and retain ownership of the relocated water utility infrastructure upon completion. The City will remain responsible for all future operation, maintenance, repairs, and restoration of any County facilities affected by future utility work within the project corridor.

CivicPlus Addendum for Asset Management – signed  9-11-26

description:
The City currently uses multiple CivicPlus products under the Multiproduct Statement of Work and Master Services Agreement approved by the City Commission through Resolution No. 2024-133. The proposed CivicPlus Statement of Work, Quote No. Q-128626-1, expands the existing platform by adding two complementary programs for the Emergency Management/Utilities Department and other participating City departments.
1. SeeClickFix 311 CRM - A resident service-request platform that allows residents to submit issues through web and mobile channels, receive status updates, and follow requests through resolution. City staff can route and assign requests, coordinate across departments, document responses, and measure request volume and performance.
2. CivicPlus Asset Management - An infrastructure and work-order management platform that centralizes asset inventories, locations, condition data, maintenance history, inspections, work orders, labor and cost information, documents, and photographs. The proposed subscription includes the core platform and modules for stormwater collection, wastewater collection, water distribution, markings, roads and streets, sidewalks, and signs.
A connector between the two programs will allow resident requests received through SeeClickFix to be coordinated with the City's asset and work-order records. This integration will reduce duplicate entry, improve communication between office and field staff, and provide a consistent record from initial request through completion.
Key anticipated benefits include:
A single, accessible channel for residents to submit and track service requests
Centralized asset inventories, condition assessments, work histories, and supporting records
Mobile access for field crews to receive assignments, complete inspections, upload photographs, and update work orders
GIS-based mapping of infrastructure assets, resident requests, and field work
Preventive-maintenance scheduling to reduce downtime and extend asset life
Improved routing, coordination, accountability, and response-time tracking
Dashboards and reports to support budgeting, capital planning, regulatory documentation, and management decisions
Unlimited government users and cloud storage, together with remote training, support, and software updates
Implementation services include data import and conversion, system configuration, GIS integration, integration between SeeClickFix and Asset Management, staff training, and go-live support. The products will be co-termed with the City's existing CivicPlus billing cycle.

description:
Zoning Application Z 25-02 is a request to rezone the subject parcel from Wilton Drive Arts and Entertainment (WDAE) to Planned Unit Development Mixed (PUD-M). PUDs are subject to development standards that are specifically established for the PUD based on the PUD Document and the approved site plan. The site plan for the proposed project consists of the demolition of an existing 48,616 square foot commercial building to be replaced with an eighty-nine (89) unit residential midrise building with a ninety-nine (99) space parking garage at the southeast corner of the parcel, two (2) new commercial buildings totaling 14,770 square feet with a new 3,850 square foot patio fronting Wilton Drive. The parking garage will consist of parking for the residential development, private storage, spa, mechanical rooms and equipment storage, trash rooms, and four (4) electrical vehicular charging stations. The existing 29,130 square foot commercial building and 4,150 square feet of patios on the northwest side of the parcel shall remain. The facade of the existing commercial building will be improved in conjunction with the new development. The subject parcel is 5.2752 net acres or 6.421 gross acres and is located at the southeast corner of Wilton Drive and NE 7 Avenue.
In accordance with Section 040-030(2) of the City’s Unified Land Development Regulations (ULDRs), PUD-M is intended for properties with residential, community facilities, Transit Oriented Corridor and or commercial land use designations; and at least two (2) uses must be approved as part of the PUD-M development. The subject parcel has a commercial land use designation, and the proposed PUD-M development is for residential and commercial uses.
The applicant has requested an allocation of eighty-nine (89) flexibility and or redevelopment units to be allocated to this project. Flexibility and or redevelopment units are allocated by the City Commission on a "first come, first served basis". The 252 flexibility units allocated to the previously approved WilMa on the Drive project will be repealed at the Second Reading of the rezoning. In addition, all previously approved agreements associated with the WilMa on the Drive project release resolutions, the flexibility and or redevelopment allocation resolution, and the resolution for a new Developer's Agreement and Declaration of Restrictive Convenants will be heard by the City Commission.
The applicant has requested fourteen (14) exceptions pursuant to Section 040-130 of the City's ULDRs. The City Commission may waive certain requirements when such requirements are not feasible or applicable to a particular property or proposed development. The applicant has provided a detailed justification of each exception.
The exceptions requested are:
Parking related -
1. Drive aisle widths within residential parking garage2. Length of existing standard parking spaces
3. Length of proposed standard parking spaces
4. Length of existing handicapped spaces
5. Length of proposed handicapped spaces
6. Width of on-street parallel parking spaces
7. Dimensional requirements for loading spaces
8. Required number of parking spaces for the residential portion of the project
9. Allowance of on-street loading spaces
Setbacks -
10. Building setback to property line abutting single-family use or zoning
11. Setback from steps to property line
12. Landscape buffer widths
Signs -
13. Number of allowable wall signs
Height -
14. Building height from five (5) stories/sixty (60) feet to six (6) stories/seventy (70) feet.
The fourteen (14) exceptions are described in detail in the staff report.
The proposed rezoning was reviewed by the Development Review Committee for consistency with the City's ULDRs including, but not limited to, Article 040 which contains the standards for PUD's. PUD standards include, a review of adequate access, provision of off-street parking and loading requirements consistent with Section 030-060 and Article 135, landscaping in accordance with Article 150, traffic consistent with Section 085-040(B)(32), minimum open space, provision for underground utilities for the project, pedestrian and bicycle circulation, energy conservation consistent with Article 170, buffering and compatibility, minimum gross acreage, and height.
The site plan, along with the PUD document, specifically describes the development standards for the proposed PUD-M. All the development standards for the PUD-M zoning are contained within the PUD Document and the approved site plan, which include, but are not limited to, height, density, setbacks, and parking requirements. The PUD Document and approved site plan will be exhibits to the zoning ordinance. attachments.name: 2026-019 ORD Authorizing First Amendment to Franchise Agreement with Coastal Waste and Recycling
First Amendment to the Franchise Agreement with Coastal Waste & Recycling of Florida, Inc. for Solid Waste & Recycling Services

description:
In 2023, the City issued Invitation to Bid (ITB) No. 2023-13 for comprehensive Solid Waste and Recycling Services. On September 12, 2023, the City Commission adopted Ordinance No. 2023-007, which designated Coastal Waste & Recycling of Florida, Inc. (Coastal) as the lowest responsive and responsible bidder, approved the Franchise Agreement (Agreement), and authorized the appropriate City officials to execute the Agreement. The Agreement incorporates the ITB, its addenda, and Coastal's bid by reference.
The initial term began October 1, 2023 and expires September 30, 2026. Section 4 of the Agreement allows the City, at its option, to renew the Agreement for two additional two-year periods on the same terms, conditions, and limitations. The proposed action would exercise the first renewal option and authorize amending the Agreement (Amendment). If approved, one additional two-year renewal option would remain available to the City for the period October 1, 2028 through September 30, 2030.
The Amendment continues to provide for residential garbage collection twice-weekly, residential recycling collection weekly, unlimited residential bulk trash collection monthly, curbside household hazardous waste collection monthly, commercial and multifamily services, roll-off services, and related ancillary services and approve the requested pricing adjustments. Renewal would maintain the existing collection framework and avoid a service transition while preserving the remaining renewal option.
RENEWAL AND RATE ADJUSTMENT ANALYSIS
During the initial three-year term, the contract rates were fixed and no price increases were permitted. Section 10.04 of the ITB permits the contractor to seek an adjustment for an extension term when supported by documentation acceptable to the Department. For the CPI component, the adjustment is based on the Consumer Price Index for All Urban Consumers for the Miami-Fort Lauderdale area and may not exceed 2.5%.
By letter dated August 14, 2026, Coastal formally requested a 2.5% increase to the contract service rates beginning October 1, 2026. Coastal's supporting calculation shows the applicable index increasing from 350.098 in December 2024 to 359.125 in December 2025, or approximately 2.58%. Because the contract caps the CPI adjustment at 2.5%, the requested adjustment does not exceed the contractual limit.
Coastal did not request the additional disposal-cost adjustment referenced in Section 10.04.
The residential core contractor rate per unit is currently $51.30; the proposed rate is $52.58; a monthly increase of $1.28.

description:
Staff is requesting authorization to fill two vacant part-time Library Page positions at the Richard C. Sullivan Public Library. These positions provide essential front-line operational support, including checking in and shelving materials, assisting at the circulation desk during peak periods, supporting library program setup, maintaining collections, and providing staffing coverage during lunch breaks and shift transitions.
The vacancies have reduced the Library’s ability to maintain consistent staffing coverage during public service hours and have placed additional responsibilities on remaining staff. This staffing shortage is further compounded by the ongoing vacancy of the full-time Library Director position. If the two Library Page positions remain unfilled, the Library may experience delays in basic library functions, inconsistent public service coverage, and difficulty maintaining its current operating hours and service levels.
Filling the two vacancies will help stabilize day-to-day operations, restore adequate front-line staffing coverage, and maintain existing library services for the public.

attachments.name: Request to Fill Position - Fire Marshal CDS 09.22.2026 CC

description:
Staff is requesting authorization to fill a vacant full-time Fire Marshal position within the Community Development Services Department. The vacancy was created through the retirement of the current employee in the position.
The Fire Marshal position is a full-time position and is responsible for the overall management and supervision of fire prevention and fire inspection activities and plays a critical role in protecting life and property within the City. The position directs, plans, organizes, and implements Fire Department activities and programs and supervises professional, technical, and support personnel involved in fire prevention, fire inspection, and related programs.
The Fire Marshal is responsible for directing inspections of buildings and other properties for fire hazards and ensuring enforcement of applicable fire prevention ordinances and laws. Maintaining appropriate staffing in this role is essential to ensuring that these responsibilities continue to be performed effectively and consistently.
Given the direct relationship between the Fire Marshal's responsibilities and the protection of life and property, filling this position is necessary to maintain effective fire prevention and inspection services, support regulatory compliance, and preserve the City's commitment to public safety.

attachments.name: 2026-057 RESO Lift Station 5 - Resilient Florida Grant

description:
The Florida Department of Environmental Protection (FDEP) administers the Resilient Florida Grant Program to support projects that address flooding and sea level rise. The City submitted an application for $942,574 toward the Lift Station No. 5 Relocation and Flood Resilience Project. The requested grant represents 50 percent of the $1,885,148 total estimated project cost.
Lift Station No. 5 is the downstream wastewater station for Lift Stations Nos. 1 through 4 and also serves its own local area. Collectively, the five service areas include 599 residential units serving approximately 988 residents, 59,482 square feet of retail and office space, a gas station, a church, a school, a 147-bed hospital, and Mickel Field Park. Continued operation of Lift Station No. 5 is therefore essential to wastewater service for a substantial portion of the community.
The City's Sea Level Rise Vulnerability Assessment identifies Lift Station No. 5 as a critical wastewater asset and projects 0.23 feet of flooding at the station under Scenario 25, which combines Category 3 storm surge, mean high tide, and the NOAA Intermediate High sea level rise projection for 2070. The service area has experienced documented flooding during four events since April 2023. Relocating and hardening the station will reduce exposure to compound flooding and improve the City's ability to maintain wastewater service during and after severe-weather events.
The project will relocate and replace Lift Station No. 5 with a new wet well, valve and meter vaults, duplex submersible pumps and a spare pump, electrical and control systems, redirected gravity sewer, force-main improvements, and associated roadway and site restoration. The improvements will provide approximately 1.08 million gallons per day of wastewater pumping capacity while reducing the risk of stormwater inflow and infiltration, equipment failure, sewage backups, sanitary sewer overflows, environmental contamination, and service interruptions. The Engineer's Opinion of Probable Construction Cost totals $1,885,148 and includes a $25,000 construction contingency, equal to 1.34 percent of the pre-contingency estimate.
Section 380.093(5)(g)3.a., Florida Statutes, and Rule 62S-8.003(4)(a), Florida Administrative Code, evaluate the availability of matching funds and provide full scoring consideration when a 50-percent cost share is available and supported by documentation specifying the committed amount or percentage. The City has secured and allocated $942,574 in available proceeds from its executed WIFIA loan. Adoption of the resolution will provide governing-board documentation endorsing the application and committing the full 50-percent City cost share if the project is selected.
The anticipated project schedule extends from March 2027 through February 2028. If funding is awarded, any grant agreement, budget amendment, procurement award, contract, or other action requiring City Commission approval will return to the Commission.

FDEP administers the Resilient Florida Grant Program under Section 380.093, Florida Statutes, to support local-government resilience planning and implementation projects that reduce risks associated with flooding and sea level rise. The City submitted an application seeking State assistance for the Stafford Park Nature-Based Shoreline and Living Seawall Project. The grant opportunity can offset a substantial portion of eligible project costs, reduce the financial burden on City taxpayers, and accelerate implementation of an identified resilience priority.
Wilton Manors is a low-lying urban community surrounded by waterways and is subject to recurring tidal flooding, intense rainfall, storm surge, shoreline erosion, and the long-term effects of sea level rise. The City's vulnerability assessment identifies exposed public assets and infrastructure and demonstrates the importance of advancing capital improvements that reduce risk, limit disruptions, and improve recovery from severe-weather events. The City's Comprehensive Plan incorporates regional sea-level-rise projections and resilience considerations, while the Wilton Manors-Oakland Park Joint Climate Action Plan provides a framework for strengthening community and infrastructure resilience in a practical and cost-effective manner.
Stafford Park is a publicly owned waterfront park that provides recreation, gathering space, public access to the City's waterways, and environmental value. The existing shoreline and seawall are vulnerable to continued deterioration, erosion, tidal conditions, and future sea-level-rise impacts. Failure to address these conditions could result in additional shoreline loss, damage to park improvements, reduced public access, increased maintenance and emergency-repair costs, and greater exposure of adjacent public property to flooding and erosion.
The proposed project will replace approximately 175 linear feet of seawall at Stafford Park with a resilient shoreline-protection system. The design will incorporate living-shoreline features where feasible, including measures that enhance shoreline stabilization, aquatic habitat, native vegetation, ecological function, and resilience to tidal flooding, erosion, storm surge, and sea level rise. The improvements are intended to stabilize and protect the City's waterfront while preserving public access and the continued recreational use of Stafford Park.
The project is expected to cost more than $1 million. Resilient Florida funding would allow the City to leverage State resources for a substantial capital improvement that otherwise would need to be funded entirely by the City or deferred. Grant funding would also support development of a more resilient, environmentally beneficial alternative than a conventional in-kind seawall replacement and would protect prior public investments in the park and adjoining facilities.
The requested Commission action is limited to endorsement of the grant application. The resolution does not approve a grant agreement, appropriate or commit matching funds, select a funding source, authorize a consultant or construction contract, or otherwise obligate the City to proceed with the project. Those matters will be presented to the City Commission if FDEP selects the project for funding.
Formal Commission endorsement documents the governing body's support for the project and confirms that the proposed investment advances a valid municipal and public purpose. The project will reduce long-term exposure to shoreline failure and flood-related damage, enhance ecological conditions, preserve public recreation and waterfront access, and strengthen the City's ability to adapt to changing coastal and climate conditions.

attachments.name: 2026-062 RESO Approving execution of Consent Order w. State of Florida Department of Environmental Protection

description:
The Florida Department of Environmental Protection (FDEP) conducted a sanitary survey of the City's public water system on September 8, 2025. Following that inspection, FDEP issued a Warning Letter dated December 12, 2025 identifying several deficiencies and possible violations of Chapter 403, Florida Statutes, and Chapters 62-550 and 62-555, Florida Administrative Code. The inspection report characterized the deficiencies as minor and noted that most of the compliance concerns resulted from missed or incomplete monitoring and reporting. The City and FDEP successfully negotiated actions required to resolve deficiency issues addressed in the Warning Letter.
The draft Consent Order (Order) dated August 27, 2026, addresses the following monitoring and reporting matters: (1) collection of the 2023 triennial Lead and Copper samples in October 2023, outside the required July-through-September sampling period; (2) late submission of monthly bacteriological monitoring reports for November 2023, December 2023, January 2024, May 2024, June 2024, September 2024, November 2024, and January 2025; and (3) late submission of quarterly Disinfection Byproducts reports for the fourth quarters of 2023 and 2024.
FDEP states in the Order that the City has completed the actions requested to resolve the violations. Accordingly, the Order does not establish any additional corrective actions. Once executed, the City is responsible for payment of civil penalties and FDEP's investigative costs. Under the proposed settlement, the City would pay $6,750 in civil penalties and $250 in investigative costs and expenses, for a total of $7,000. The attached penalty calculation worksheet attributes $3,000 to the Lead and Copper monitoring matter and $3,750 to monitoring-report submittals, with an additional $250 for Department costs.
Acceptance of the Consent Order will fully resolve the pending FDEP enforcement matter. The City's acceptance does not constitute an admission of liability. Once the Consent Order is countersigned and filed by FDEP, it will become a final agency order. As part of the settlement, the City will waive its rights to an administrative hearing and appeal regarding the terms of the final order.
The signed Order must be returned to FDEP to be counter-signed and recorded, which will then constitute the final order. Payment is due in full within 30 days after the effective date of the final order. Approval of the resolution will authorize the Mayor to execute the Consent Order and allow staff to complete payment and the related administrative actions within the required timeframes.

First Amendment to the Franchise Agreement with Coastal Waste & Recycling of Florida, Inc. for Solid Waste & Recycling Services

description:
In 2023, the City issued Invitation to Bid (ITB) No. 2023-13 for comprehensive Solid Waste and Recycling Services. On September 12, 2023, the City Commission adopted Ordinance No. 2023-007, which designated Coastal Waste & Recycling of Florida, Inc. (Coastal) as the lowest responsive and responsible bidder, approved the Franchise Agreement (Agreement), and authorized the appropriate City officials to execute the Agreement. The Agreement incorporates the ITB, its addenda, and Coastal's bid by reference.
The initial term began October 1, 2023 and expires September 30, 2026. Section 4 of the Agreement allows the City, at its option, to renew the Agreement for two additional two-year periods on the same terms, conditions, and limitations. The proposed action would exercise the first renewal option and authorize amending the Agreement (Amendment). If approved, one additional two-year renewal option would remain available to the City for the period October 1, 2028 through September 30, 2030.
The Amendment continues to provide for residential garbage collection twice-weekly, residential recycling collection weekly, unlimited residential bulk trash collection monthly, curbside household hazardous waste collection monthly, commercial and multifamily services, roll-off services, and related ancillary services and approve the requested pricing adjustments. Renewal would maintain the existing collection framework and avoid a service transition while preserving the remaining renewal option.
RENEWAL AND RATE ADJUSTMENT ANALYSIS
During the initial three-year term, the contract rates were fixed and no price increases were permitted. Section 10.04 of the ITB permits the contractor to seek an adjustment for an extension term when supported by documentation acceptable to the Department. For the CPI component, the adjustment is based on the Consumer Price Index for All Urban Consumers for the Miami-Fort Lauderdale area and may not exceed 2.5%.
By letter dated August 14, 2026, Coastal formally requested a 2.5% increase to the contract service rates beginning October 1, 2026. Coastal's supporting calculation shows the applicable index increasing from 350.098 in December 2024 to 359.125 in December 2025, or approximately 2.58%. Because the contract caps the CPI adjustment at 2.5%, the requested adjustment does not exceed the contractual limit.
Coastal did not request the additional disposal-cost adjustment referenced in Section 10.04.
The residential core contractor rate per unit is currently $51.30; the proposed rate is $52.58; a monthly increase of $1.28.

description:
The City issued Request for Proposals (RFP) No. 2026-05 seeking proposals for the operation and management of the City's parking system. Following receipt of proposals, a three-member Selection Committee, consisting of Darren Brodsky, Assistant Chief of Police; Dio Sanchez, Human Resources Director/Risk Manager; and Michelle Parks, Leisure Services Director, independently evaluated and scored each proposal using the evaluation criteria published in the RFP. Based on the combined technical and pricing scores established under the solicitation, ACE Parking III, LLC ("ACE") was identified as the highest-ranked proposer, and the City issued a Notice To Award.
On July 6, 2026, LAZ Parking ("LAZ"), an unsuccessful proposer, filed a formal written protest challenging the intended award. Procurement notified ACE of the protest and provided an opportunity to submit a response. Procurement conducted a comprehensive review of the protest, the solicitation documents, the submitted proposals, and the evaluation record.
Ace subsequently submitted a written response to the protest, which is included in the agenda packet for the Commission’s consideration.
LAZ's protest raises four principal allegations:
• ACE does not satisfy the RFP's requirement for an established management base in Florida;
• ACE's pricing proposal was based on fewer parking assets than required by the solicitation;
• ACE's proposal contains boilerplate language and conditional references to parking technology that allegedly render its proposal non-responsive; and
• The evaluation committee improperly scored the proposals because LAZ received higher technical scores while ACE received the highest overall score due to pricing.
Procurement reviewed each allegation against the requirements of the RFP, the submitted proposals, the Selection Committee's evaluation record, and the procurement file. As detailed in the attached Procurement Memorandum, staff concluded that none of the protest allegations establish that ACE's proposal was non-responsive, that the three-member Selection Committee failed to follow the published evaluation criteria, or that the intended award was inconsistent with the terms of the solicitation.
Staff further determined that the evaluation was conducted in accordance with the evaluation criteria published in the RFP and that the resulting rankings properly reflected the combined technical and pricing evaluations established by the solicitation.
Accordingly, Procurement recommends that the protest be denied and that the intended award to ACE Parking III, LLC be upheld.
title: Discussion of Bid Protest submitted by Laz Florida Parking LLC

description:
The City of Wilton Manors has been awarded a Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA) Hazard Mitigation Grant Program (HMGP) award, administered by the Florida Division of Emergency Management (FDEM), for the preparation of a Citywide Watershed Master Plan. The grant provides $150,000 in federal funding toward a total project cost of $200,000, with the required 25% non-federal match ($50,000) being satisfied through documented in-kind City staff services
The Watershed Master Plan will provide the City with a comprehensive technical evaluation of its drainage system and watershed conditions to better understand and address flooding caused by heavy rainfall, tidal influences, sea level rise, elevated groundwater, and aging stormwater infrastructure. The planning effort will include hydrologic and hydraulic modeling for multiple storm events, identification of flood-prone areas, evaluation of future climate conditions, assessment of existing infrastructure, development of mitigation strategies, and preparation of a prioritized implementation plan. The completed plan will also support the City's participation in the National Flood Insurance Program (NFIP) Community Rating System (CRS) and future updates to the Broward County Local Mitigation Strategy.
The project is expected to benefit the entire City by improving long-term flood resilience for approximately 11,788 residents, while supporting 4,195 flood insurance policies, including 1,868 policies located within Special Flood Hazard Areas. The resulting Watershed Master Plan will serve as a roadmap for future capital improvements, strengthen the City's competitiveness for state and federal infrastructure funding, and provide technical guidance for future stormwater planning, resilience initiatives, and regulatory compliance. The planning effort is intended to reduce future flood risks while enhancing the City's ability to adapt to changing environmental conditions.
The grant agreement has a performance period from March 11, 2026, through May 31, 2028, and is administered as a cost-reimbursement grant through the Florida Division of Emergency Management.

Consulting Agreement with Ardurra Group Wilton Manors signed

description:
The City maintains approximately 35.6 miles of gravity sewer pipes and 830 sewer manholes. Wastewater enters this public system through approximately 4,400 privately owned sewer laterals. These structures may crack or fracture over time, allowing rainwater and ground water to seep into the sanitary sewer system as Infiltration and Inflow (I&I). Excess I&I consumes valuable wastewater treatment capacity and increases the City's costs for wastewater conveyance and treatment. Preliminary evaluations indicate that approximately 0.8 million gallons per day of groundwater and stormwater may be entering the City's sanitary sewer system. Reducing these flows can improve system reliability, extend infrastructure life, defer future capital improvements, and reduce long-term operating costs borne by utility customers.
On April 1, 2026, the City received an Unsolicited Proposal for a City-Wide I&I Reduction Program to detect and remove extraneous groundwater and rainwater from the sewer system. The proposed I&I reduction program includes program administration; data collection and evaluation to include flow monitoring, Sanitary Sewer Evaluation Survey (SSES), manhole inspections, smoke testing, and other field and engineering tasks, and compiling of rehabilitation and repair packages.
An initial assessment determined the proposal satisfies the submission requirements of Florida Statute §255.065 and review and meets the statutory definition of a project serving a public purpose such that it should proceed to evaluation under the unsolicited proposal process. On April 28, 2026, the City Commission approved Resolution 2026-025, providing notice of intent, pursuant to section 255.065, Florida statutes to enter into a Comprehensive Agreement for a qualifying project to perform a Sanitary Sewer Evaluation Survey (SSES), manhole inspection, smoke testing and other field and engineering tasks for a citywide Infiltration & Inflow reduction program, and notice of intent to accept other proposals for the same project.
The public notice established a deadline of June 23, 2026 for the submission of competing proposals for the same project. No other proposals were received by the deadline, and the sole proposal was evaluated based on five criteria:
Technical Approach & Understanding
Relevant Experience & Qualifications
Cost Effectiveness & Value
Project Management & Schedule
Public Benefit & Community Impact
On July 14, 2026, the evaluation was presented to the City Commission. Based on the evaluation of the proposal received and consideration of the public benefits associated with the project, the City Commission authorized the City Manager to negotiate and execute a Comprehensive Agreement with the highest-ranked proposer, Ardurra Group, Inc.

description: Article 030 of the City’s Unified Land Development Regulations (ULDRs) includes the City of Wilton Manors’ definitions, regulations, and development requirements for the City’s Urban Center Mixed-Use Districts which are defined as the Wilton Drive Arts and Entertainment District (WDAE), Transit-Oriented Corridor North District (TOC-N), Transit-Oriented Corridor South District (TOC-S), Transit-Oriented Corridor East District (TOC-E), and Transit-Oriented Corridor West District (TOC-W). The purpose of the Urban Center Mixed-Use Districts is to encourage and facilitate the development of a mixture of residential units, entertainment, cultural facilities, restaurants, shopping, commercial, retail, and professional office uses. The City Commission has directed city staff to amend Article 030 to reflect Commission priorities as well as to incorporate feedback received from the community and developers. The proposed amendments include, but are not limited to, changes to alcohol distance separation requirements for establishments, definitions, permitted and prohibited uses, absolute maximum height, building design provisions, off-street parking requirements, and signage requirements.

description:
Zoning Application Z 25-02 is a request to rezone the subject parcel from Wilton Drive Arts and Entertainment (WDAE) to Planned Unit Development Mixed (PUD-M). PUDs are subject to development standards that are specifically established for the PUD based on the PUD Document and the approved site plan. The site plan for the proposed project consists of the demolition of an existing 48,616 square foot commercial building to be replaced with an eighty-nine (89) unit residential midrise building with a ninety-nine (99) space parking garage at the southeast corner of the parcel, two (2) new commercial buildings totaling 14,770 square feet with a new 3,850 square foot patio fronting Wilton Drive. The parking garage will consist of parking for the residential development, private storage, spa, mechanical rooms and equipment storage, trash rooms, and four (4) electrical vehicular charging stations. The existing 29,130 square foot commercial building and 4,150 square feet of patios on the northwest side of the parcel shall remain. The facade of the existing commercial building will be improved in conjunction with the new development. The subject parcel is 5.2752 net acres or 6.421 gross acres and is located at the southeast corner of Wilton Drive and NE 7 Avenue.
In accordance with Section 040-030(2) of the City’s Unified Land Development Regulations (ULDRs), PUD-M is intended for properties with residential, community facilities, Transit Oriented Corridor and or commercial land use designations; and at least two (2) uses must be approved as part of the PUD-M development. The subject parcel has a commercial land use designation, and the proposed PUD-M development is for residential and commercial uses.
The applicant has requested an allocation of eighty-nine (89) flexibility and or redevelopment units to be allocated to this project. Flexibility and or redevelopment units are allocated by the City Commission on a "first come, first served basis". The 252 flexibility units allocated to the previously approved WilMa on the Drive project will be repealed at the Second Reading of the rezoning. In addition, all previously approved agreements associated with the WilMa on the Drive project release resolutions, the flexibility and or redevelopment allocation resolution, and the resolution for a new Developer's Agreement and Declaration of Restrictive Convenants will be heard by the City Commission.
The applicant has requested fourteen (14) exceptions pursuant to Section 040-130 of the City's ULDRs. The City Commission may waive certain requirements when such requirements are not feasible or applicable to a particular property or proposed development. The applicant has provided a detailed justification of each exception.
The exceptions requested are:
Parking related -
1. Drive aisle widths within residential parking garage2. Length of existing standard parking spaces
3. Length of proposed standard parking spaces
4. Length of existing handicapped spaces
5. Length of proposed handicapped spaces
6. Width of on-street parallel parking spaces
7. Dimensional requirements for loading spaces
8. Required number of parking spaces for the residential portion of the project
9. Allowance of on-street loading spaces
Setbacks -
10. Building setback to property line abutting single-family use or zoning
11. Setback from steps to property line
12. Landscape buffer widths
Signs -
13. Number of allowable wall signs
Height -
14. Building height from five (5) stories/sixty (60) feet to six (6) stories/seventy (70) feet.
The fourteen (14) exceptions are described in detail in the staff report.
The proposed rezoning was reviewed by the Development Review Committee for consistency with the City's ULDRs including, but not limited to, Article 040 which contains the standards for PUD's. PUD standards include, a review of adequate access, provision of off-street parking and loading requirements consistent with Section 030-060 and Article 135, landscaping in accordance with Article 150, traffic consistent with Section 085-040(B)(32), minimum open space, provision for underground utilities for the project, pedestrian and bicycle circulation, energy conservation consistent with Article 170, buffering and compatibility, minimum gross acreage, and height.
The site plan, along with the PUD document, specifically describes the development standards for the proposed PUD-M. All the development standards for the PUD-M zoning are contained within the PUD Document and the approved site plan, which include, but are not limited to, height, density, setbacks, and parking requirements. The PUD Document and approved site plan will be exhibits to the zoning ordinance. The following changes have been made to the site plan based on the recommended conditions by approval of the Planning and Zoning Board from the June 16, 2026, meeting. description:
The City issued Request for Proposals (RFP) No. 2026-05 seeking proposals for the operation and management of the City's parking system. Following receipt of proposals, a three-member Selection Committee, consisting of Darren Brodsky, Assistant Chief of Police; Dio Sanchez, Human Resources Director/Risk Manager; and Michelle Parks, Leisure Services Director, independently evaluated and scored each proposal using the evaluation criteria published in the RFP. Based on the combined technical and pricing scores established under the solicitation, ACE Parking III, LLC ("ACE") was identified as the highest-ranked proposer, and the City issued a Notice To Award.
On July 6, 2026, LAZ Parking ("LAZ"), an unsuccessful proposer, filed a formal written protest challenging the intended award. Procurement notified ACE of the protest and provided an opportunity to submit a response. Procurement conducted a comprehensive review of the protest, the solicitation documents, the submitted proposals, and the evaluation record.
Ace subsequently submitted a written response to the protest, which is included in the agenda packet for the Commission’s consideration.
LAZ's protest raises four principal allegations:
• ACE does not satisfy the RFP's requirement for an established management base in Florida;
• ACE's pricing proposal was based on fewer parking assets than required by the solicitation;
• ACE's proposal contains boilerplate language and conditional references to parking technology that allegedly render its proposal non-responsive; and
• The evaluation committee improperly scored the proposals because LAZ received higher technical scores while ACE received the highest overall score due to pricing.
Procurement reviewed each allegation against the requirements of the RFP, the submitted proposals, the Selection Committee's evaluation record, and the procurement file. As detailed in the attached Procurement Memorandum, staff concluded that none of the protest allegations establish that ACE's proposal was non-responsive, that the three-member Selection Committee failed to follow the published evaluation criteria, or that the intended award was inconsistent with the terms of the solicitation.
Staff further determined that the evaluation was conducted in accordance with the evaluation criteria published in the RFP and that the resulting rankings properly reflected the combined technical and pricing evaluations established by the solicitation.
Accordingly, Procurement recommends that the protest be denied and that the intended award to ACE Parking III, LLC be upheld.
title: Discussion of Bid Protest submitted by Laz Florida Parking LLC

attachments.name: Request to Fill Position - Customer Service Representative CDS 8.25.2026 CC-COWMHAG01A

description:
Staff is requesting authorization to fill a vacant full-time Customer Service Representative position within the Community Development Services Department. The vacancy was created through the resignation of the current employee in the position.
The Customer Service Representative is a full-time position responsible for providing daily customer service and administrative support to the public and the Community Development Services Department.
The Customer Service Representative is responsible for responding to public and business inquiries; assisting with permitting and business licensing; maintaining departmental records; providing information regarding departmental processes; greeting visitors; and performing related administrative functions. These responsibilities are essential to ensure that residents, businesses, contractors, and applicants receive timely, accurate, and professional assistance.
Filling this position is important to maintain effective customer service and efficient departmental operations. Leaving the position vacant increases wait times for customers and places additional demands on existing staff, requiring employees with other technical and professional responsibilities to absorb routine customer service and administrative functions. Filling the position will help maintain service levels, improve the efficiency of permitting and licensing processes, and allow existing staff to remain focused on their primary technical and professional responsibilities.
title: Request to Fill Full-Time Customer Service Representative Vacancy

2026-049 RESO Approving Crossing Guard Services Agreement with Nextaff

description:
The existing agreement with The Butler Group of South Florida, LLC d/b/a NEXTAFF expired July 16, 2026, following the conclusion of the 2025-2026 summer school year session. The Wilton Manors Police Department requests approval to enter into a new agreement with NEXTAFF for school crossing guard services to ensure the continued safety of students traveling to and from school.
Pursuant to the Agreement and the School Crossing Guard Services Proposal dated July 1, 2026, NEXTAFF shall furnish four (4) qualified crossing guards, to staff four (4) designated crossing guard posts within the City for two (2) hours per day during the 180-day regular school year, plus up to thirty (30) additional days for summer school, if offered at a school in Wilton Manors.
If approved, the Agreement shall commence on August 10, 2026, and continue through the last day of the 2027–2028 Broward County Public Schools academic year, including summer school schedules, if applicable. The agreement may be renewed by the City for two (2) additional two-year terms.
The current post locations:
POST LOCATIONS | WILTON MANORS
Northeast 26th Street and Northeast 6th Avenue
Northeast 26th Street and Northeast 3rd Avenue
Northeast 24th Street and North Andrews Avenue

description:
The City of Wilton Manors was awarded $77,996 through the Broward County Community Development Block Grant (CDBG) Program for the installation of above-ground lighting along the existing crosswalk on Powerline Road north of NW 24th Street.
The City issued Invitation to Bid (ITB) No. 2026-06 on January 23, 2026, with bids due on March 3, 2026. Two bids were received in response to the solicitation.
Following review of the bids, the apparent low bidder, On The Line Electric, was determined to be non-responsive because its bid package contained an incomplete Attachment F – Certification Pursuant to Florida Statutes Section 287.135, and the required Attachment I – Anti-Human Trafficking Affidavit was not submitted. In an effort to confirm whether the omission was inadvertent, City staff contacted the bidder and requested that the missing documentation be provided. The bidder did not respond to the City's request and did not submit the required documents. Accordingly, the bid was determined to be non-responsive and was not eligible for award.
Horsepower Electric, Inc. submitted the next lowest responsive and responsible bid in the amount of $94,400.00. The Broward County Housing Finance and Community Development Division, which administers the CDBG Program, reviewed the procurement and authorized the City to proceed with award to Horsepower Electric, Inc.

Case File Packet - Lien Reduction Request

description:
Executive Summary
A request for a lien reduction was submitted by the property owner, Simply Delish, LLC via attorney Nemia Schulte for the property located at 2500 Wilton Drive, Wilton Manors, FL 33305. In this agenda item are the case file documents, application for lien reduction request, a lien reduction appeal packet, and the Magistrate’s ruling brief. The property owner, Simply Delish, LLC was the owner of the subject property at the time of the violation(s).
At the January 8, 2025, Magistrate Hearing the subject property was found ‘In Violation’ of the violation(s) cited.
The property owner was given until April 27, 2025, to comply or face a $250.00 per day fine.
Compliance was not achieved within the ordered time prompting the case to be heard at the May 7, 2025 Magistrate Hearing where the fines were certified.
The lien(s) was recorded with Broward County on May 9, 2025.
The property was determined to be “in compliance” on November 22, 2025, meaning the property was “non-compliant” for 209 days x’s $250.00 equaling a total lien amount of $52,250.00.
At the March 4, 2026 lien reduction hearing, the Magistrate reduced the lien by 50% to $27,731.31.
Magistrate Ruling Brief Summary
The current owners of Simply Delish LLC took the necessary action to bring the violations into compliance after recovering ownership of the property from the previous owner. The length of time before the ordered compliance date and the date of the violation was eliminated was approximately 209 days, during which time the current owners were unable to initiate compliance with the city code until a foreclosure was begun against the previous owner, which eventually allowed the current owners to regain ownership of the property based on the failure of the prior owner to pay the seller financing.
Through information provided by legal counsel and Ms. Bartolome, the evidence reflected the property had been sold with seller financing which eventually ended up in foreclosure when the purchaser failed to pay the mortgage and the property was returned to the prior owners of Simply Delish LLC, Ms. Bartolome and Ms. Karen Samra. During the period of ownership by another, the property deteriorated and the owner installed canopies without obtaining required permits, which resulted in the current violations. Since the property was returned to the current owners of Simply Delish, LLC, no income has resulted for the owners and expenses have been incurred to bring the property back into compliance with the Code at a cost of at least $5,000.00. The property is currently for sale though there is no contract pending and the 16 code violations have been brought into compliance as of 11/22/2025.
City Staff Response to Applicant’s Information Provided
Code compliance staff mailed the notice of violation to the address of the Simply Delish, LLC registered agent's office. There is signed confirmation of receipt. The notice of violation was posted on the property. According to BCPA records the owner Simply Delish, LLC took ownership of the property on November 5, 2024. This was recorded with the Broward County Commission November 26, 2024. Although the case was opened October 28, 2024 the notice of violation is dated November 26, 2024 and was mailed the same day. The confirmation of receipt was signed November 29, 2024. The notice of violation was also posted on the property on November 27, 2024.

attachments.name: 2026-046 RESO PROPOSED OPERATING MILLAGE RATE GENERAL OP FY 2026-2027

description:
This budget proposes an ad valorem operating millage rate of 6.2270, the same rate as the current fiscal year’s rate. This proposed millage rate represents an increase of 4.07% over the rolled-back millage rate of 5.9835 due to an increase in city-wide taxable values of 4.73% based on the Broward County Property Appraiser’s (BCPA’s) July 1 certified property values.
The proposed voted debt service millage rate for the 2008 City Hall Bond has decreased from 0.1661 for Fiscal Year 2025-26 to 0.1598 for Fiscal Year 2026-27 (-0.0063 mils, -3.8%) also due to the increase in property taxable values.
The overall city-wide millage rate, combining the operating and debt service rates, will decrease in FY2026-27 by 0.0063 mils, or 0.1%. The FY 2025-26 overall millage rate was 6.3931; the proposed FY2027 overall millage rate is 6.3868.
The City's budgeted operating ad valorem revenues for Fiscal Year 2026-27, as adjusted by the expected collection rate (96%), are $15,436,308. This amount is based on the Broward County Property Appraiser's (BCPA's) July 1 certified property taxable values, and is $20,162 more than the amount published on Jun 29 in the Proposed (Recommended) Budget.
For homesteaded property under the Save Our Homes amendment, Florida state statutes limit the increase in assessed value to 3% or the percentage of the change in the Consumer Price Index (CPI) for the preceding calendar year. This year, the Florida Department of Revenue set the maximum increase for homesteaded property at 2.7% for Fiscal Year 2026-27 property tax rates.
Section 200.065(5), Florida Statutes limits the amount a government may increase its millage rate with a simple majority vote of the governing body. A complicated formula is used to calculate this limitation - see Draft Form DR420-MMP in the backup. Due to this restriction, the maximum millage rate the City Commission may approve this year by a majority vote (3 votes) is 5.9835. A two-thirds vote (4 votes) may approve a millage rate up to 6.5819. A unanimous vote is required to approve any millage rate between 6.5820 and the statutory cap of 10.
This resolution authorizes the City Commission to advise the Property Appraiser about the following items which will be included in the City's TRIM (Truth In Millage) notices for the Fiscal 2026-27 budget:
a. Proposed Operating Millage Rate of 6.2270
b. Proposed Rolled-Back Millage Rate of 5.9835
c. Proposed Voted Debt Service Millage Rate of 0.1598 for the 2008 City Hall Bond
d. The first public hearing to consider the budget and millage rates is scheduled for
September 14, 2026, at 6:30 pm in the City Commission Chambers.

description:
The City maintains approximately 35.6 miles of gravity sewer pipes and 830 sewer manholes. Wastewater enters this public system through approximately 4,400 privately owned sewer laterals. These structures may crack or fracture over time, allowing rainwater and ground water to seep into the sanitary sewer system as Infiltration and Inflow (I&I). Excess I&I consumes valuable wastewater treatment capacity and increases the City's costs for wastewater conveyance and treatment. Preliminary evaluations indicate that approximately 0.8 million gallons per day of groundwater and stormwater may be entering the City's sanitary sewer system. Reducing these flows can improve system reliability, extend infrastructure life, defer future capital improvements, and reduce long-term operating costs borne by utility customers.
On April 1, 2026, the City received an Unsolicited Proposal for a City-Wide I&I Reduction Program to detect and remove extraneous groundwater and rainwater from the sewer system. The proposed I&I reduction program includes program administration; data collection and evaluation to include flow monitoring, Sanitary Sewer Evaluation Survey (SSES), manhole inspections, smoke testing, and other field and engineering tasks, and compiling of rehabilitation and repair packages.
An initial assessment determined the proposal satisfies the submission requirements of Florida Statute §255.065 and review and meets the statutory definition of a project serving a public purpose such that it should proceed to evaluation under the unsolicited proposal process. On April 28, 2026, the City Commission approved Resolution 2026-025, providing notice of intent, pursuant to section 255.065, Florida statutes to enter into a Comprehensive Agreement for a qualifying project to perform a Sanitary Sewer Evaluation Survey (SSES), manhole inspection, smoke testing and other field and engineering tasks for a citywide Infiltration & Inflow reduction program, and notice of intent to accept other proposals for the same project.
The public notice established a deadline of June 23, 2026 for the submission of competing proposals for the same project. No additional proposals were received by the deadline, and the proposal was evaluated based on five criteria:
Technical Approach & Understanding
Relevant Experience & Qualifications
Cost Effectiveness & Value
Project Management & Schedule
Public Benefit & Community Impact
These criteria were selected to evaluate the overall value, feasibility, public benefit, and ability of each proposer to successfully implement the City's I&I Reduction Program. Based on the evaluation of the proposals received and consideration of the public benefits associated with the project, staff recommends that the City Commission authorize the City Manager to execute a Comprehensive Agreement with the highest-ranked proposer.

The Wilton Manors Police Department seeks to partner with PropertyRoom.com, Inc. to provide auction and asset disposition services for surplus property, high-liability items and unclaimed or abandoned property, and evidence authorized for disposal in accordance with applicable laws and departmental procedures, Chapter 705, Florida Statutes, and applicable CFA Chapter 27 property and evidence standards.
PropertyRoom.com, Inc. is a nationwide online auction and property and asset disposition company that specializes in assisting law enforcement agencies with the management and disposal of unclaimed, found, forfeited, seized, surplus and evidentiary property. The company has served more than 4,400 law enforcement and municipal agencies throughout the United States for over 20 years.
PropertyRoom.com provides a full-service solution by managing the entire auction process, including asset pickup, secure transportation, inventory tracking, chain-of-custody documentation, item preparation, online auction marketing, payment processing, shipping, and reporting. The service supports accountability, audit readiness, and lawful property disposition while reducing evidence room storage demands and administrative workload. In addition, the acquisition of these services support recommendations made by the Center for Police Management, LLC (CPSM), who is currently conducting an organizational assessment, to dedicate additional resources to the purging of items in the property and evidence room.
PropertyRoom.com, Inc. was awarded Sourcewell Contract No. 111424 through a competitive solicitation process for Auction Services with Related Solutions. Sourcewell is a governmental cooperative purchasing organization whose competitively awarded contracts may be utilized by the City to procure goods and services in accordance with applicable purchasing requirements.

description:
The BFAS agreement provides the Wilton Manors Police Department (WMPD) with access to the Florida Department of Highway Safety and Motor Vehicles FLHSMV driver's license photographs for biometric facial comparison purposes. The system is intended to generate investigative leads and may be used in criminal investigations, missing person cases, identifying individuals unable to communicate their identity, and other law enforcement purposes. BFAS search results are considered investigative leads only and do not constitute a positive identification or probable cause without independent investigative corroboration.
Use of BFAS will continue to be governed by departmental policy, which establishes authorized users, permissible uses, privacy protections, training standards, and safeguards against misuse. The policy also limits the use of facial recognition technology to only legitimate law enforcement purposes, prohibits real-time surveillance and discriminatory use, and requires documentation, supervisory oversight, and periodic audits of system activity.
Approval of this agreement will provide WMPD with a continued investigative resource while ensuring compliance with applicable state and federal privacy laws, including the Driver's Privacy Protection Act (DPPA), and departmental standards for accountability, security and protection of civil liberties.
