attachments.name: 2026-044 RESO Strategic Planning Consultant Agreement with BerryDunn

description:
The attached Agreement is between the City of Wilton Manors and Berry, Dunn, McNeil & Parker, LLC for the provision of Strategic Planning Consulting Services.
The City conducted a formal competitive solicitation through Request for Proposals (RFP) No. 2026-09 in accordance with the City's Procurement Code. The solicitation was publicly advertised on the City's website and through DemandStar to encourage broad competition. At the close of the solicitation, nine (9) proposals were received from qualified firms.
The Selection Committee evaluated the proposals based on the criteria established in the RFP. All nine (9) proposers were invited to provide oral presentations and respond to questions from the Selection Committee. Upon completion of the evaluation process, Berry, Dunn, McNeil & Parker, LLC received the highest overall score and was determined to be the top-ranked proposer. Staff subsequently entered into negotiations with the top-ranked firm and successfully negotiated the attached agreement.
Under the agreement, the consultant will facilitate the development of a comprehensive Strategic Plan that will establish the City's long-term organizational priorities and guide future decision-making. The scope of services includes stakeholder and community engagement, evaluation of City services and facilities, assessment of organizational strengths and opportunities, sustainability and community identity initiatives, development of strategic goals and implementation strategies, alignment with the City's operating and capital budgeting processes, establishment of performance measures and key performance indicators (KPIs), and preparation and presentation of the final Strategic Plan for adoption by the City Commission.
The agreement provides for a total compensation not to exceed $57,900. Services will commence upon issuance of a Notice to Proceed and are expected to be completed within eight (8) months, resulting in a final Strategic Plan ready for implementation by April 2027. The agreement contains the City's standard provisions regarding insurance, indemnification, record retention, ownership of work products, audit rights, termination, and compliance with applicable federal, state, and local laws.
Approval of this agreement will authorize the City Manager to execute the contract with Berry, Dunn, McNeil & Parker, LLC and proceed with the development of the City's Strategic Plan.

description:
Staff is requesting authorization to fill a vacant full-time Administrative Coordinator position within the Emergency Management/Utilities Department following the departure of the current employee. The position provides essential administrative and technical support for the Department, including procurement and contract administration, budget tracking, records management, regulatory reporting, project coordination, customer service, and support for emergency management operations.
The Administrative Coordinator serves as the Department's primary administrative support role and is critical to maintaining continuity of utility operations, capital improvement projects, regulatory compliance, and emergency preparedness activities. Staff advises that failure to fill the position would reduce administrative capacity, delay procurement and invoice processing, impact regulatory reporting and project coordination, and diminish customer service and operational efficiency.
The position is fully funded through existing Enterprise Fund revenues, with personnel costs allocated among the Solid Waste and Recycling, Sewer, and Water Utilities. Filling the vacancy will help ensure continuity of operations and maintain the level of service expected by residents and stakeholders.
title: Request to Fill Full-Time Administrative Coordinator Vacancy

attachments.name: Environmental Program Specialist Vacancy Request Commission Memorandum

description:
Staff is requesting authorization to fill a vacant full-time Environmental Program Specialist position within the Emergency Management/Utilities Department. The vacancy was created through the reclassification of the former Capital Projects & Grants Administrator position following the retirement of Todd DeJesus.
The Environmental Program Specialist is responsible for managing Citywide environmental compliance and regulatory programs related to water, wastewater, stormwater, floodplain management, and right-of-way operations. Primary responsibilities include administration of environmental permits and regulatory reporting requirements; management of the City's National Pollutant Discharge Elimination System (NPDES) Program; drinking water and wastewater regulatory compliance; drainage reviews and permitting; floodplain management; right-of-way permitting and inspections; and administration of the City's streetlight program.
The position was established to address the growing workload associated with regulatory compliance, environmental permitting, floodplain management, and utility program administration while providing dedicated staff support for drainage reviews and environmental permitting. Failure to fill this position would increase the risk of missed regulatory deadlines, diminished program oversight, and potential compliance violations. Filling the vacancy is essential to maintaining compliance with federal, state, and local regulatory requirements while advancing the City's environmental stewardship, infrastructure management, and resilience objectives.
The position is fully funded through existing Enterprise Fund revenues, with personnel costs allocated among the Road Improvement, Stormwater, Sewer, and Water Utility Funds. Authorizing the recruitment and hiring of this position will ensure continuity of operations, maintain regulatory compliance, and sustain the level of service expected by residents and stakeholders.
title: Request to Fill Full-time Environmental Program Specialist ​Vacancy

attachments.name: 2026-036 RESO Approving First and Second Amendment to ILA for Solid Waste Disposal and Recyclable Materials Processing Authority
ILA Solid Waste Disposal and Recycable Materials Processing Authority Broward County 4_25_2023
First Amendment to ILA (Final Facilities Amendment)

description:
The proposed resolution authorizes approval of the First Amendment (Facilities Amendment) and the Second Amendment to the Interlocal Agreement (ILA) for the Solid Waste Disposal and Recyclable Materials Processing Authority of Broward County (the “Authority”). The ILA, approved by the City Commission on April 25, 2023, established a regional framework for coordinating solid waste disposal, recycling, and diversion services among Broward County and participating municipalities. The Authority was created to address increasing waste generation, limited disposal capacity, evolving regulatory requirements, and the need for a sustainable and cost-effective long-term regional waste management strategy.
The Facilities Amendment is a required “Formation Condition” under the ILA and is necessary for the Authority to continue operating beyond August 15, 2026. The Facilities Amendment establishes the legal and operational framework for implementation of the regional solid waste system, including long-term contingency planning for waste disposal capacity, governance and limitations on Authority-owned facilities, protection of public assets, and detailed procedures governing the orderly transfer of services, facilities, and assets in the event the Authority is dissolved. The amendment also clarifies the types of facilities the Authority may own and operate, establishes safeguards to promote transparency and accountability, and creates a structured wind-down process intended to avoid the disputes and uncertainty that occurred following the dissolution of Broward County's previous regional solid waste system.
In conjunction with the Facilities Amendment, the Authority has adopted a Comprehensive Master Plan that establishes a long-term roadmap for solid waste management in Broward County. The Master Plan focuses on reducing reliance on landfills, expanding recycling and diversion programs, harmonizing disposal and processing services across participating jurisdictions, developing regional infrastructure, enhancing public education and outreach, and leveraging economies of scale to achieve greater operational efficiency and long-term cost stability.
The proposed Second Amendment provides participating municipalities with additional flexibility by establishing two future opportunities to withdraw from the Authority. The first withdrawal option allows a municipality to withdraw within forty-five (45) days following the Executive Committee's recommendation of contract awards resulting from the Authority's regional procurement process for municipal solid waste disposal, recycling processing, and yard waste processing services, which is anticipated to occur in 2027. This provision allows participating municipalities to evaluate actual service costs before making a longer-term commitment to the regional system. The second withdrawal option allows municipalities to withdraw effective August 16, 2048, provided notice is submitted by August 16, 2047. The Second Amendment also establishes procedures governing the effects of withdrawal and provides that if municipalities representing more than twenty percent (20%) of the participating municipal population withdraw, the Governing Board may initiate dissolution of the Authority pursuant to the wind-down procedures established in the Facilities Amendment.
From a financial perspective, participation in the Authority is structured in phases. For the City of Wilton Manors, the estimated Phase I (FY 2027) contribution is approximately $14,845, based on population, which is comparable to current funding levels. Subsequent phases transition to a system funded through modest per-ton surcharges and, ultimately, a non-ad valorem assessment structure intended to provide long-term cost predictability while supporting regional infrastructure investments, recycling initiatives, and system improvements.
Approval of the Facilities Amendment and Second Amendment will allow the City to remain a participating member of the Authority, support implementation of the Master Plan, preserve future withdrawal options should regional costs or local priorities change, and continue collaboration with Broward County and neighboring municipalities to address long-term solid waste disposal, recycling, and diversion needs.

Eagle Wilton Manors - SUP Request for Alcohol Sales Hours Extension (GB146-060926)

description:
Spartacus NightClubs LLC, doing business as Eagle Wilton Manors, located at 2209 Wilton Drive, has submitted a Specific Use Permit Application, requesting an extension of the hours to serve and sell alcoholic beverages in accordance with Section 3-9(f) of the City of Wilton Manors ("City") Code of Ordinances ("Code"). Section 3-9(f) of the City’s Code governs the hours during which alcoholic beverages may be sold, served, or delivered and process for requesting an extension of these hours. No person, vendor, or employee of a state-licensed vendor may sell, offer for sale, deliver, or serve any liquor, beer, or wine regardless of alcohol contact on Monday through Friday between the hours of 2:00 a.m. and 7:00 a.m., and on Saturday and Sunday between the hours of 3:00 a.m. and 7:00 a.m. Section 3-9(f) states that the request and/or approval of an exemption shall not exceed past 4:00 a.m. The extended hours requested by Eagle Wilton Manors are as follows:Monday, September 7, 2026 from 2:00 a.m. to 4:00 a.m.
Sunday, November 29, 2026 from 3:00 a.m. to 4:00 a.m.
City staff have reviewed the request to ensure consistency with Section 3-9(f) of the City's Code, which includes, but is not limited to, the City of Wilton Manor's Comprehensive Plan, the City's Unified Land Development Regulations, impacts on traffic circulation, impacts on pedestrian safety, nuisance factors, screening and buffering of adjacent property, neighborhood scale and character, and whether off-duty sworn officers are required.
City staff is recommending approval of the extension request for the below dates with the condition that the sale and service of alcoholic beverages and the consumption of these alcoholic beverages are limited to the inside of the bar (bricks and mortar), with no outside sale, service or consumption and off-duty detail officers are required. Two off-duty detail Wilton Manors police officers per extension are required to enhance safety and security at the event, mitigate/eliminate the need for on-duty police resources to be utilized if a need arises, and align with department policy. The applicant must coordinate with the Police Department's contracted partner 60 days prior to the date of each extension to hire off-duty detail officers for the hours of 12:00 am - 4:00 am. For more information, please refer to the police department's memorandum attached to this item.

Monday, September 7, 2026 from 2:00 a.m. to 4:00 a.m.
Sunday, November 29, 2026 from 3:00 a.m. to 4:00 a.m.

description:
Wicked Manors is one of the City’s largest and most anticipated annual events, drawing significant regional attendance to Wilton Drive and generating economic activity for local businesses and the community. The 2025 event brought an estimated 40,000 people to the City.
The Pride Center at Equality Park is requesting approval to host the 2026 Wicked Manors Halloween Street Festival on Saturday, October 31, 2026, from 6:00 p.m. to 11:00 p.m. along Wilton Drive. The permit provides for the closure of Wilton Drive beginning at 9:00 a.m. on October 31, 2026, through 4:00 a.m. on November 1, 2026.
In advance of the event, City staff will continue to coordinate with the Pride Center’s organizing team on logistics, public safety, permitting, site plan review, parking operations, and event requirements. Coordination will include review by the Special Event Committee, public safety planning, emergency access, vendor layout, accessibility, sanitation, alcohol permitting, severe weather procedures, and post-event cleanup requirements.
Consistent with prior years and the terms of the 2026 Special Event Permit, the City will provide planning guidance and coordination assistance related to the event. The City has budgeted $8,000 for barricades and road closure costs associated with the event. The City will also waive building permit fees associated with the event, estimated at $2,500.
The City will provide staff support for permit coordination, Special Event Committee meetings, review of the event site plan and operational planning documents, and related logistical support. Any direct City labor costs and associated benefits for event set-up, equipment assistance, and related labor services requested by the Pride Center will be reimbursed to the City by the Pride Center.
The Pride Center will be responsible for all public safety and emergency medical services costs, security screening, vendor coordination, alcohol permitting, trash removal, post-event cleanup, and compliance with all applicable permit conditions. The Pride Center will also be responsible for reimbursing the City for invoiced direct costs associated with logistical support within 30 days after the event.
The permit further provides that the City will contribute parking revenues collected from Saturday, October 31, 2026, at 4:00 a.m. through Sunday, November 1, 2026, at 4:00 a.m., less all direct and indirect costs incurred by the City related to parking management, enforcement, staffing, equipment, administration, and contractor services associated with the event.
title: Motion to approve Special Event Permit for Wicked Manors

description:
On July 9, 2019, the City Commission approved a Memorandum of Understanding (MOU) with Broward County confirming the City’s desire to participate in the establishment and implementation of an integrated regional solid waste and recycling system (Resolution 2019-055).
Beginning in February 2020, a series of meetings were held to discuss the operational needs for a Countywide solid waste system, its associated costs, and the development of an Interlocal Agreement (ILA) to govern the system
On January 25, 2022, the City Commission approved the First Amendment to the MOU (Resolution 2022-007) which defined the City and County roles for the execution and funding of a Waste Generation Study, Waste Composition Study, and other related consultant services required to establish and fund the solid waste and recycling system.
On April 25, 2023, The City Commission approved the ILA to join the Solid Waste Disposal and Recyclable Materials Processing Authority of Broward County (Resolution 2023-039). The ILA required the membership to adopt a Master Plan and Facilities Amendment developed by the Authority and establishes financial contributions from the City towards its operations.
On June 13, 2023, the City Commission repealed Resolution 2023-039 following changes by Broward County to the agreement and approved a new ILA to join the Solid Waste Disposal and Recyclable Materials Processing Authority of Broward County (Resolution 2023-054). The ILA required the membership to adopt a Master Plan and Facilities Amendment developed by the Authority and establishes financial contributions from the City towards its operations. There was a requirement that seventy-five percent (75%) of the County’s total population had to be represented by municipalities approving the ILA.
On August 7, 2023, the City was informed that twenty-eight (28) municipalities representing eighty-three percent (83%) of the County’s population approved the ILA, establishing the BSWA.
At the March 20, 2026, BSWA Governing Board meeting, the First Amendment (the Facilities Amendment) was approved by the Governing Board. At the April 17, 2026, BSWA Governing Board meeting, the Master Plan was approved by the Governing Board. The next steps are for Broward County and at least two-thirds (2/3) of the participating municipalities to approve the Facilities Amendment. The Facilities Amendment must be approved by the County and municipalities representing at least eighty percent (80%) of the population (of the participating municipalities). Both approval conditions must be met, with the Facilities Amendment being the final condition for the BSWA to meet formation requirements. The deadline for the Master Plan and Facilities Amendment approval is August 15, 2026.
At the June 15, 2026 BSWA Governing Board meeting, the Second Amendment to the ILA was approved by the Governing Board. The Second Amendment provides participating municipalities with additional flexibility by establishing two future opportunities to withdraw from the Authority.
Representatives from the Broward Solid Waste Authority (BSWA) will provide the City Commission with an update on its Master Plan and Facilities Amendment.
title: Broward County Solid Waste Authority to Provide the City Commission with an Update on its Master Plan and Amendments to the Interlocal Agreement

description:
The City’s current contract with CrowderGulf Joint Venture, Inc. for disaster debris removal services is set to expire on July 10, 2026. In anticipation of this expiration and to ensure continuity of services, the City issued Request for Proposals (RFP) #2026-07 for Disaster Debris Removal and Disposal Services on February 26, 2026.
A total of six (6) proposals were received in response to the RFP. An Evaluation Committee was established to review, evaluate, and rank the proposals based on established criteria. All six proposals were determined to be responsive.
Following a comprehensive evaluation process, DRC Emergency Services, LLC was ranked as the top proposer. The Evaluation Committee unanimously recommends DRC Emergency Services, LLC for award of the contract.
Maintaining a pre-event debris removal contract is critical to ensuring the City’s ability to respond quickly and efficiently to storm events and other disasters, particularly in advance of the 2026 hurricane season.

description:
The City Commission is requested to approve a Commercial Fire and Burglar Alarm Monitoring, Inspection, and Emergency Services Agreement and accompanying Addendum with Alpha Security & Fire Alarm Services, Inc. for fire alarm monitoring, burglar alarm monitoring, annual inspections, testing, and emergency maintenance services at various City facilities.
In October 2025, the City issued ITB 2026-01 for fire and security alarm services. The bids received were determined to be cost prohibitive and were subsequently rejected. Staff reviewed the scope of work, refined service requirements, and solicited quotes from multiple qualified vendors. Following evaluation of the proposals received, Alpha Security & Fire Alarm Services, Inc. was determined to be the lowest responsive and responsible vendor and is recommended for award.
Under the agreement, Alpha Security will provide burglar alarm monitoring services at Hagen Park, Richardson Park, Stafford Park, the Library, and Mickel Park; fire alarm monitoring services at Hagen Park, Stafford Park, City Hall/Police Station, and the Library; annual fire alarm inspections and testing; and emergency maintenance and repair services as needed. The annual cost for recurring monitoring and inspection services is $8,720, with emergency repair services performed on an as-needed basis at the contract rates established in the agreement.
In addition to the operational services provided under this agreement, the FY 2026 Capital Improvement Program includes $30,597 for alarm system upgrades and equipment replacement at various City facilities. Staff's assessment identified several deficiencies within the existing fire and security alarm systems, including aging sensors and devices, obsolete equipment, and fire alarm communicators that continue to rely on legacy landline technology rather than modern cellular communication methods. These upgrades are necessary to improve system reliability, address equipment that has reached the end of its useful life, and bring facilities into compliance with current fire and life-safety code requirements.
The agreement provides for an initial three-year term with two one-year renewal options upon mutual agreement of the parties. The accompanying Addendum incorporates the City's standard contractual provisions, including public records requirements, insurance requirements, cybersecurity protections, termination for convenience, and other municipal contracting requirements.
Approval of this agreement will ensure continued monitoring, testing, inspection, maintenance, and modernization of critical life-safety and security systems throughout City facilities while supporting ongoing code compliance efforts and protecting City assets, staff, and visitors.

attachments.name: Wilton Manor PD - PowerDMS Expansion Quote - Jul '26_2
Resolution No. 2025-022 Addendum Services Agreement GovernmentJobs.com Inc. dba NeoGov for Powerpolicy Professional Subscription

description:
The Wilton Manors Police Department currently utilizes PowerDMS PowerPolicy subscription for policy management, policy distribution, electronic attestation, and accreditation compliance pursuant to Resolution No. 2025-022 approved by the City Commission in March 2025.
The Police Department is seeking approval to expand the PowerDMS platform through the addition of the following Software as a Service (SaaS) modules:
PowerReady – Field training and employee onboarding management system designed to standardize training, automate documentation, track trainee progress in real time, and reduce administrative workload for supervisors and Field Training Officers (FTOs). This acquisition would align with an initial recommendation from the Center for Public Safety Management, LLC, who is currently conducting an organizational assessment of the police department.
PowerAction – On-duty action reporting system that streamlines documentation and review of use of force incidents, vehicle pursuits, vehicle crashes, and other operational reports through automated workflows, real-time dashboards, and electronic approval processes. Although not specifically recommended by the Center for Public Safety Management, LLC, this high liability-related module complements and supports the capabilities provided through the PowerReady and PowerIA modules, creating a clear nexus between these integrated systems.
PowerIA – Internal Affairs and complaints management platform that centralizes investigations, complaint tracking, audit trails, and professional standards workflows while improving accountability, confidentiality, and supervisory oversight. This acquisition would align with an initial recommendation from the Center for Public Safety Management, LLC, who is currently conducting an organizational assessment of the police department.
Key benefits to the Police Department and the community served include:
Reduction in paper-based processes and administrative workload
Improved accountability, documentation, and audit tracking
Enhanced supervisory oversight through real-time dashboards and analytics
Faster report review, approvals, and training documentation retrieval
Improved compliance with accreditation and reporting requirements
Centralized and secure storage of training, investigative, and performance records, including role-based access controls and audit trails for records management
Single sign-on access and workflows that improve operational efficiency through one integrated platform across divisions
Better data analytics and reporting for leadership decision-making
Enhanced coordination between policies, training, and investigations
Improved transparency and consistency in professional standards oversight
Stronger risk management and liability reduction through improved documentation and compliance tracking
The PowerDMS expansion quote provides discounted pricing through a multi-year subscription structure and includes a one-time setup and implementation services for each module. These services include system configuration assistance, implementation consultants, training instructions, access to online resources and user guides, software updates, and ongoing technical support and maintenance.
title: Motion to approve additional Software as a Service subscriptions with PowerDMS d/b/a NEOGOV

attachments.name: 2026-029 RESO Approving Construction Agreement with FDOT for 50th CDBG Project

description: Resolution 2024-040 authorized the City to submit a grant application for the 50th Year Community Development Grant (CDBG) Program. The City of Wilton Manors was awarded $77,996 for the installation of above-ground lighting along the existing crosswalk on Powerline Road north of NW 24 Street. To construct the project, the City must complete a Construction Agreement with the Florida Department of Transportation (FDOT) to authorize installation of the CDBG-funded crosswalk lighting improvements within FDOT right-of-way. The agreement allows the City to construct the project in accordance with FDOT standards and subject to FDOT review and approval of all plans, while assigning the City full responsibility for permitting, utility coordination, construction engineering inspection, traffic control, safety compliance, and adherence to all applicable regulations. The City must complete construction within 365 days, and submit as-built plans and certification upon completion, after which the improvements will be owned and maintained by FDOT. FDOT retains oversight authority, including the right to halt work for safety or non-compliance and to enforce corrective actions if necessary.

description:
The City issued Invitation to Bid (ITB) No. 2026-02 for the purchase and installation of a new emergency generator at Hagen Park. The project is intended to enhance the resiliency and operational continuity of Hagen Park by ensuring an uninterrupted power supply during emergency situations and power outages.
The City Engineer, Chen Moore and Associates, was tasked with preparing the technical specifications for the project and assisting staff with the review and evaluation of the bids received in response to the solicitation.
The City received three (3) bids in response to ITB No. 2026-02. Following the review of the bids submitted, the lowest and most responsive and responsible bidder became non-responsive and subsequently withdrew its proposal from consideration.
Staff subsequently reviewed the second-lowest bid and conducted a detailed evaluation of the bidder's qualifications, experience, and references. Based on the bid review and results of reference checks, staff determined that Cavan Electric, Inc. demonstrated the qualifications, experience, and capacity necessary to successfully perform the required work and satisfy the City's project requirements.

attachments.name: Village Toyota 2025 RAV FSA Contract Quote_04.16.26

description:
The Police Department seeks Commission approval for the purchase of two (2) 2025 Toyota RAV4 LE vehicles at a total of $60,364.00. The proposed vehicles are LE trim models, representing the manufacturer's standard configuration, and were selected as the most cost-effective option that meets operational and safety requirements. These vehicles will be assigned to the Detective Bureau and will replace two (2) unmarked vehicles that have reached the end of their useful lifespan due to model year, mileage, crash history, mechanical condition and overall appearance.
Projected vehicles to be replaced are a 2017 Ford Explorer (VIN #1FM5K7B87HGC25851) and a 2017 Ford Fusion (VIN #3FA6POLU8JR125209). This purchase complies with the City's current vehicle capital replacement plan, and includes a standard factory 36-month/36,000-mile basic coverage and 60-month/60,000-mile powertrain and safety restraint warranties. Attachments include detailed quotations from Village Cadillac Toyota, and specifications for the standard LE front-wheel drive model.
If approved, the Police Department will proceed with the immediate purchase of two (2) 2025 Toyota RAV4 from Village Cadillac Toyota, that are readily available for purchase and delivery. Securing the 2025 models will help ensure the vehicles will be outfitted and ready for service by early summer 2026.
If approved for purchase, both vehicles will be procured under the Hillsborough County Sheriff's Office Florida Sheriffs Association (FSA) Cooperative Purchasing Program, Host Contract FSA-HCS-AVP1.0: Assorted Vehicle Procurement. The contract is available to eligible state and local government agencies from October 28, 2024, through October 27, 2028, and ensures compliance with all FSA contractual terms and conditions. Village Cadillac Toyota is one of the 17 vendors awarded under this Host Sheriff Procurement Contract in accordance with Chapter 30 and Chapter 163, Florida Statutes, and best practices articulated in Chapter 287, Florida Statutes.
title: Motion to approve the purchase of two (2) unmarked police vehicles for the Police Department.

description: City staff proposes an amendment to Section 045-060, “Pools, decks and screen enclosure” of the City’s Unified Land Development Regulations (ULDRs) to allow for twenty-five (25) percent pervious credit for pool overflow drains when legally installed. A pool overflow drain is a drain installed at the maximum desired water level of a pool. When rain, filling, or splash-out raises the water above that level, the excess water flows into the overflow drain. The water is then routed to an underground or above-ground retention area which will allow the excess water from the pool to seep into the soil and refill underground aquifers. A pool overflow drain is a drain installed at the maximum desired water level of a pool. Section 045-050 of the City’s ULDRs contains the setback requirements for pools, decks, screen enclosures, and roofed structures, and permanent safety barrier requirements for pools. City staff conducted a review of land development regulations in comparable jurisdictions, consulted with pool contractors, and analyzed zoning reviews of historical pool permits to inform the proposed amendment to Section 045-060 of the City’s ULDRs. The twenty-five (25) percent pervious credit would be discounted from the square footage associated with the impervious surface area of the pool. In order to obtain credit, the applicant would be required to submit signed and sealed engineering drawings demonstrating that the pool overflow drain will drain into an underground or above ground retention area mitigating the impervious surface area equal to the size of the proposed pool when applying for a building permit where the minimum pervious requirement for the applicable zoning district must be satisfied.

description:
The United States Environmental Protection Agency (EPA), under the Federal Water Pollution Control Act (“Clean Water Act”) and related regulations, requires compliance with the National Pollutant Discharge Elimination System (NPDES) Municipal Separate Storm Sewer System (MS4) Permit Program. The EPA delegated the NPDES permitting program to the Florida Department of Environmental Protection (FDEP).
Under the purview of FDEP and acting as the “lead permittee”, Broward County (County), through its Public Works and Environmental Services Department (PWESD), coordinates and conducts specific technical activities required by the NPDES MS4 Permits (Permits) along with (26) participating Municipalities acting as “co-permittees.” Previous Interlocal Agreements (ILA) were executed on December 3, 1996, October 20, 1998, June 29, 2004, and May 7, 2013, to carry out tasks required by the Permit. The current ILA for the Cycle 4 Permit, executed November 7, 2017, will expire upon issuance of the Cycle 5 Permit on or about October 1, 2026, and continue for a period of five (5) years.
The City wishes to continue the County’s services of coordinating with the co-permittees pursuant to the NPDES MS4 regulations, and managing and performing technical tasks necessary to comply with the Permit. Co-permittees will continue to pay an annual fee to the County, based on 2020 population census figures, as prescribed in ‘Exhibit B’ of the ILA.

description:
The Emergency Management/ Utilities Department requests authorization to fill a Utilities Technician I position following the resignation of the incumbent effective May 18, 2026. The Utilities Technician I is a full-time position responsible for the maintenance and repair of the City’s drainage system, streets, and rights-of-way infrastructure. Duties include cleaning, inspecting, and repairing catch basins, stormwater pipes, and drainage structures; repairing or replacing damaged or undersized drainage components; performing minor roadway repairs such as pothole patching and surface restoration; and installing and maintaining sidewalks, curbs, and related infrastructure. The position also installs, repairs, and replaces street signs, pavement markings, and traffic control devices, and assists with street striping operations.
The Utilities Technician I position is a critical field operations role that directly supports the maintenance of the City’s drainage system, streets, and rights-of-way infrastructure throughout Wilton Manors. This is one of only two positions assigned to the Streets and Drainage Division; therefore, this vacancy represents a significant reduction in the City’s ability to perform essential maintenance and emergency response functions.

description:
The City maintains approximately 33.5 miles of roadway and seeks to complete a comprehensive pavement condition survey to support long-term maintenance planning and prioritize roadway funding. The proposal from WGI, Inc. provides a citywide pavement condition assessment using advanced laser-based technology (LCMS 4M) to collect detailed roadway data and evaluate surface distresses such as cracking, rutting, and potholes. This data will be analyzed to generate Pavement Condition Index (PCI) scores for roadway segments and incorporated into a GIS-based platform for mapping and visualization. The resulting PCI data will also be used to develop cost estimates and prioritize future roadway resurfacing and rehabilitation projects.
Project deliverables include GIS datasets with PCI values linked to roadway centerlines and an interactive ArcGIS dashboard, which will be hosted for two years. The project is anticipated to be completed within approximately 120 days from notice to proceed. Staff is asking the City Commission to ratify and waive the competitive procurement requirements of Section 2-58 of the City code and to authorize entering into an agreement with WGI, Inc. for a lump sum of $27,920.

260406 Wastewater System Evaluation - Scope of Services

description:
The Final Judgment associated with Consent Order 20-1436 resolves an enforcement action initiated by the Florida Department of Environmental Protection (FDEP) regarding the City’s wastewater collection system, including sanitary sewer overflows (SSOs) and reporting requirements. As part of the Final Judgment, the City is required to retain a professional engineer registered in the State of Florida to conduct a comprehensive evaluation of the wastewater collection and transmission system.
This evaluation must be completed and submitted to FDEP within 270 days of the effective date of the Final Judgment. Failure to complete this evaluation within the required timeframe may result in additional regulatory enforcement, including fines and mandated corrective actions.
The required evaluation includes, but is not limited to:
Verification of daily and monthly wastewater flows conveyed through Master Lift Station No. 11 during calendar year 2025
Assessment of the discharge capacity of the City’s existing force main connections to the City of Fort Lauderdale system
Evaluation of proposed improvements to Master Lift Station No. 11
Identification and analysis of system alternatives to ensure adequate capacity and reduce the potential for future sanitary sewer overflows
If the evaluation determines that existing infrastructure is insufficient to convey peak flows, the City must also assess the feasibility of system improvements, including additional force main connections or other infrastructure modifications. The City will subsequently be required to select a preferred alternative and submit an implementation schedule to FDEP.
Chen Moore and Associates (CMA) has submitted a proposal to perform these required engineering services for a total fee of $104,175. CMA’s scope includes data collection and evaluation, system capacity analysis, coordination with regulatory and partner agencies, and preparation of a final Wastewater System Evaluation Report.
Based on the results of this evaluation, CMA will prepare a separate scope of services for the design, permitting, and implementation of any required system improvements. These improvements will need to be completed on an expedited schedule to meet FDEP compliance deadlines.

description:

description:
The City maintains approximately 35.6 miles of gravity sewer pipes and 830 sewer manholes. Wastewater enters this public system through approximately 4,400 privately owned sewer laterals. These structures may crack or fracture over time, allowing rainwater and groundwater to seep into the sanitary sewer system as Infiltration and Inflow (I&I). On April 4, 2026, the City received an Unsolicited Proposal for a City-Wide I&I Reduction Program to detect and remove extraneous groundwater and rainwater from the sewer system. The proposed I&I reduction program includes program administration, data collection and evaluation to include flow monitoring, Sanitary Sewer Evaluation Survey (SSES), manhole inspections, smoke testing, and other field and engineering tasks, and compiling of rehabilitation and repair packages.
An initial assessment has determined that the proposal satisfies the submission requirements of Florida Statute §255.065 for purposes of initial intake and review and meets the statutory definition of a project serving a public purpose such that it should proceed to evaluation under the unsolicited proposal process. The proposal provides sufficient detail beyond a conceptual level and addresses a qualifying wastewater infrastructure project that serves a clear public purpose.

attachments.name: Utilities Project Manager Commission Memorandum Feb 26 2026

description:
The Emergency Management and Utilities Department requests authorization to create a Utilities Project Manager position to provide dedicated oversight and administration of the City’s water, wastewater, and stormwater utility projects. The role would be responsible for managing all phases of project delivery, from planning and design through construction and compliance, while ensuring projects are completed on time, within budget, and in accordance with municipal, state, and federal requirements. This position is particularly important given the increasing complexity of infrastructure projects and the need for dedicated coordination, oversight, and regulatory compliance.
The request is largely driven by the City’s participation in the Water Infrastructure Finance and Innovation Act (WIFIA) program, which includes a $29 million loan supporting approximately $37 million in infrastructure improvements. These projects require extensive documentation, financial tracking, and federal compliance, making a dedicated project manager essential to mitigate risks and ensure successful delivery. Funding for the position would be allocated across the utility enterprise funds and partially offset through eligible project costs, including WIFIA-related expenditures. Overall, staff believes this position will enhance project efficiency, reduce reliance on external services, and support the City’s long-term infrastructure reliability and resiliency goals.

description:
During the 2nd CDBG Public Hearing on March 24, 2026, the City Commission determined that improvements to the existing splash pad at Mickel Park would best meet the CDBG criteria and serve a community need.
Additional background information:
The City's anticipated allocation of Community Block Grant dollars for the 52nd year funding cycle is approximately $75,000. However, this amount is not guaranteed. As the Commission is aware, the primary objective of CDBG funds is to assist low to moderate income persons or neighborhoods to improve their quality of life. This may be achieved by development of social programs or through infrastructure improvements.
CDBG funds have been utilized in the past to rebuild a lift station, construct sidewalks and a drainage system, and resurface streets in the Highland Estates neighborhood. Funds have also been utilized to construct estate style fencing, the installation of an emergency generator, construction of a floating dock, the construction of an addition to the community center building, installation of an artificial turf surface on the playground and a shade structure on the rear deck, the installation of outdoor physical fitness stations, a shade structure over the fitness stations, the expansion of the basketball court and improvements to an adjacent pavilion and the installation of security cameras at Island City Park Preserve (ICPP). Funds have also been used for the construction of a facility maintenance building at Mickel Park, drainage improvements on the west side, and new LED lighting at Hagen Park.
It was suggested at previous public hearings that consideration be given to the development of programs to benefit low income residents including possible computer training programs. Unfortunately, Broward County has advised the City that no new social service programs may be funded with 52nd year allocations. This is due to the limitation by HUD regulations that such programs may not exceed fifteen percent of the total allocations to all cities throughout the county. Existing programs already meet that maximum allowed level and in fact, due to the substantial reduction in funding to all the cities, some existing social service programs have had to be cut back to stay within the fifteen percent cap.
Staff received project input at two public hearings, emails from residents, and discussions with neighborhood associations. Projects recommended included the lighting along Wilton Drive, a decorative sign pole at Wilton Drive/NE 6th Avenue, a dog park at Donn Eisele, fencing at Donn Eisele park, and lighting at Rachel Richardson Park.

Piggyback Agreement (FLL) with David Mancini & Sons, Inc. for Stormwater Improvements - Executed by DMSI

description:
The City of Wilton Manors has an ongoing need to improve stormwater conveyance and reduce localized flooding within low-lying residential neighborhoods. The Coral Gardens Drive and NE 27th Drive area, adjacent to Lieber Park, experiences significant flooding during heavy rainfall events. As a result, the City has identified this corridor for targeted stormwater system improvements to enhance capacity, improve outfall protection, and provide better overall resiliency. The proposed Coral Gardens Drive & NE 27th Drive Stormwater Improvements project includes the installation of approximately 800 linear feet storm drain pipe, new drainage structures, construction of new Type C ditch bottom inlets, installation of a new 4-foot diameter manhole, and connection to the existing manhole system. In addition, the project includes installation of an 18-inch WaStop inline tidal check valve to prevent backflow from the adjacent canal during high tide events with a pollution retardant baffle to enhance water quality.
David Mancini & Sons, Inc. has submitted a total price proposal of $384,064.00 to complete the improvements. The pricing is based on unit rates established under a City of Fort Lauderdale piggyback agreement for Annual General Stormwater Contract (ITB Event No. 468-1), ensuring cost consistency and market competitiveness.
Upon completion, the improvements are expected to significantly enhance stormwater collection and conveyance capacity within the project area, reduce roadway and yard flooding during storm events, and minimize tidal backflow impacts from the Middle River. These upgrades will increase system reliability, protect adjacent residential properties and public infrastructure, and further the City’s ongoing efforts to strengthen stormwater resilience in vulnerable neighborhoods.

description:
The implementation of a new access control system is essential to improving the organization’s overall security posture and operational efficiency. The proposed system provides several key advantages over the current solution, which was installed during the original construction of City Hall more than 15 years ago. The new system features a cloud-based architecture and full integration with the security camera system installed in 2025, delivering significant operational and security benefits.
The cloud-based design enables faster and more flexible system management. Security administrators can make real-time updates, adjust access permissions, and monitor activity without needing to be physically on site or rely on legacy hardware. This capability allows the organization to respond more quickly and consistently to potential security incidents, reducing risk and improving incident response times. Additionally, the cloud platform provides improved scalability, automatic updates, and enhanced system reliability.
In addition, the new Motorola access control system integrates seamlessly with the security camera infrastructure installed last year. This integration creates a unified security environment in which access events can be automatically correlated with video footage. By combining these data sources, staff gain improved situational awareness, streamlined investigative capabilities, and more accurate incident verification. This integration strengthens overall security while also reducing the time and effort required for staff to review and respond to security events. This purchase is made through a piggyback on the competitively procured agreement between Sourcewell and Motorola. The agreement between Sourcewell, 202 12th Street Northeast, P.O. description:
Senate Bill 954, codified as Chapter 2025-182 or Florida Statutes 397.487, requires the adoption of an ordinance establishing application procedures for the owner of a “recovery residence” to request reasonable accommodation from any local land use regulation. The proposed amendments to Section 010-030, Section 020-070, Section 020-120, and Section 175-030 of the City's ULDRs include the addition of definitions; changes to the permitted, conditional, and prohibited use tables; and modifications to the reasonable accommodation ordinance.
The proposed ordinance was approved subject to final review and approval by the City Attorney by the Planning and Zoning Board. The following is a summary of changes that were made to the proposed ordinance since the February 9, 2026, Planning and Zoning Board Meeting:Language was added to specific provisions "8" in Section 020-070(B) and Section 020-120(B) that states "City staff will endeavor to determine whether an applicant for reasonable accommodations meets the distance requirement, but may require applicant to provide proof of distance from one or more existing recovery residences in the form of documentation prepared by a professional land surveyor".
Language was added to Section 175-030(F) that allows for the City to impose a cost recovery fee for actual costs incurred by the City to process a reasonable accommodation application based on the fee established and amended by the Resolution of the City Commission.

description:
The City of Wilton Manors hosts numerous mass gathering events throughout the year, including its signature events, the Stonewall Pride Festival and Parade and the Wicked Manors Halloween Festival, which attract approximately 35,000 to 50,000 attendees. In addition, the City supports a variety of other community events, such as the Farmer's Market, Flea Market, Car Show, and Rock the Block, collectively serving more than 90,000 participants annually.
To enhance public safety and mitigate risks associated with both accidental and intentional vehicular intrusion, the Police Department is proposing a phased acquisition of U.S. Department of Homeland Security (DHS) "SAFETY Act Designated Modular Vehicle Barrier System (MVB3X), Certified to ASTM F2656-15 and related standards. These systems are designed to stop high-impact vehicle threats, including semi-tractor trailers, and are widely used nationwide to secure large public events.
The proposed system includes a 72-unit modular barrier package with a dedicated transport trailer, allowing for rapid deployment and flexible configuration across various roadway widths. The barriers are lightweight, foldable, and can be deployed or repositioned by a single operator without tools. Additional features include quick lane access, multi-terrain capability, integrated gate functionality, high-visibility lighting, and zero maintenance requirements.
Currently, the City has relied on the Broward Sheriff's Office (BSO) for access to a limited number of barrier systems; however, future use will be subject to availability and setup fees. Approval of this item will significantly improve the safety of residents, visitors, City staff, and law enforcement personnel during large-scale public gatherings.
The cost for one fully equipped system, including trailer and accessories, is $198,458. Based on current event participation, this equates to approximately $2.20 per attendee. A multi-year approach is proposed to expand coverage and enhance protection across City events.

description:
The Wilton Manors Police Department seeks City Commission approval to authorize the disbursement of $1,000 from the Law Enforcement Forfeiture Trust Fund (LEFTF) to the Lucky Lightyear Foundation Inc.

The requested funding will support the “A Call to Keep” Black LGBTQ+ Leaders Summit, a community-focused leadership and public safety convening to be held in Wilton Manors. The summit will bring together local and national leaders to engage in collaborative dialogue centered on neighborhood safety, violence reduction, and community-based prevention strategies. By fostering proactive engagement, cross-sector collaboration, and community-driven solutions, the initiative supports the development of safer neighborhoods and aligns with the statutory purposes of the Law Enforcement Trust Fund.
The Chief of Police certifies that this expenditure meets the criteria set forth under Florida State Statutes, Chapter 932, Section 932.7055. This expenditure also aligns with the objectives of the Law Enforcement Forfeiture Trust Fund (LEFTF) by fostering community trust, enhancing police-community relations and supporting proactive crime prevention through inclusive outreach.

The organization trains and deploys professional therapy dog teams to provide structured, evidence-informed intervention focused on emotional regulation, stress reduction, and crisis prevention. Services are delivered to diverse populations, including young people, individuals experiencing homelessness, survivors of violence, individuals facing mental health or substance-use challenges, and first responders.
The requested funding will support the organization's Animal-Assisted Therapy Program within Wilton Manors. By proactively addressing stress and trauma-related responses, these services align with the City's public-safety objectives, support crime prevention efforts, and may reduce the need for emergency law enforcement intervention.

description:
The City’s anticipated allocation of Community Block Grant dollars for the 52nd year funding cycle (2026/2027) is estimated at $76,000. The primary objective of CDBG funds is to assist low to moderate income persons or neighborhoods to improve their quality of life. This may be achieved by developing social programs or through infrastructure improvements. According to the socio-economic data collected by the county, the eligible neighborhoods in Wilton Manors for capital or infrastructure improvements are in the southwest and south central areas in the City.
CDBG funds have been utilized in the past to re-build the sewage lift station, construct sidewalks and a drainage system, and resurface streets in the Highland Estates neighborhood. Funds have also been utilized to improve Stafford Park , including the construction or installation of estate style fencing, an emergency generator, a 35-foot floating dock, an addition to the community center building, an artificial turf surface on the playground, a shade structure on the rear deck, fitness station, a shade structure over the fitness station, a basketball court renovation, and security cameras. Funds have also been utilized to acquire and develop the property adjacent to Stafford Park at 811 N.E. 28th Street. More recently, funds were allocated for improvements to the existing ball field and a new storage and maintenance facility building at Mickel Park and drainage improvements on the west side of the City. The first phase of energy efficient lighting installations at Hagen Park was recently completed.
Broward County has advised that no new social service programs, such as possible computer training, will be funded with CDBG funds. This is due to the limitation by HUD regulations that such programs may not exceed fifteen percent of the total allocations to all cities through the county. Existing programs already meet that maximum allowed level and, in fact, due to the substantial reduction in funding to all the cities, some existing social service programs have had to be cut back to stay within the fifteen percent cap.
This public hearing provides an opportunity to receive input from residents. This is the second public meeting being held for the 52nd Year CDBG program. At the conclusion of this hearing, the Commission will select a project for Commission approval based on public input and the parameters of the grant application.
title: CDBG 52nd Year Discussion and Project Selection

Recycling, Solid Waste & HHW Coord. Description

description:
The Emergency Management/Utilities Department is seeking authorization to fill the vacant Recycling, Solid Waste & HHW Coordinator position following the resignation of a long-tenured employee. This role is integral to the administration and oversight of the City’s solid waste, recycling, and household hazardous waste programs. Responsibilities include managing the City’s collection contract, ensuring regulatory compliance, monitoring service performance, resolving service issues, coordinating hazardous waste events, and serving as the primary liaison between residents, the collection contractor, and the Utility Billing Division.
This position is critical to maintaining essential public health services, regulatory compliance, and the quality of life for residents. Without dedicated oversight, the City could experience service disruptions, increased complaints, and potential contractual or environmental challenges. The Coordinator also supports emergency response operations and can assist with broader utility functions when needed. The position is fully funded through the Recycling and Solid Waste Enterprise Fund and does not impact the General Fund. The Department intends to fill the role through internal promotion to preserve institutional knowledge and ensure continuity of service, and requests authorization to backfill any resulting vacancy to maintain operational staffing levels.
title: Request to Fill Full-Time Recycling, Solid Waste and HHW Coordinator Vacancy

attachments.name: LS Memo for Summer Rec Leaders

description:
Leisure Services requests approval to hire three Seasonal Recreation Leader I positions to support the City’s Summer Camp program, as included in the FY26 budget. The program runs for nine weeks during the summer and serves up to 50 children daily, providing structured recreational activities, enrichment programming, and field trips in a safe and supervised environment. Seasonal staff are scheduled for approximately 14 weeks to allow for pre-camp training, program preparation, active camp operations, and post-camp wrap-up. These positions are essential for supervising campers, assisting with daily activities, and maintaining appropriate staffing levels to ensure safety and smooth program operations. Financially, the program has historically generated positive net revenue while covering operating costs and staffing expenses.
If these positions are not filled, the City would not be able to safely operate the Summer Camp program at its current capacity. The program would likely need to be significantly scaled back to serve fewer participants with reduced hours, resulting in lower revenue and limited service to families. Additionally, existing transportation arrangements are based on full enrollment, meaning a reduced program would be inefficient and could lead to financial losses. Without adequate staffing, the City may not be able to operate a Summer Camp program. Approval of these positions will allow recruitment and onboarding to begin in time for the upcoming summer season.
title: Request to Fill Part-Time Summer Recreation Leader Vacancies

attachments.name: Updates to Section 7-14 to Address Disaster Response Meals

description:
The Florida Recovery Obligation Calculation (F-ROC) process was established to assist applicants in assessing the risk of potential non-compliance within the FEMA Public Assistance (PA) Program. The City, under the leadership of the Utilities/Emergency Management Department, recently performed a city-wide Disaster Readiness Assessment. F-ROC reviewed our assessment and issued an abatement plan outlining steps the City can take to increase our overall score and strengthen compliance, thereby increasing reimbursement potential should we experience a natural disaster and seek FEMA funding.
There were many areas where the City’s overall score could be increased. One such area involved documenting disaster response meals in the City’s personnel handbook/policy. This update to the Personnel and Safety Rules and Regulations adds the F-ROC-recommended language regarding meals for employees participating in disaster response activities.
The City moves to update Section 7-14, Emergency Compensation Policy, to include the F-ROC language below:
E. Disaster Response – Meals
Meals will be provided to all employees and volunteers who are engaged in eligible Emergency Work, including those assigned to or working at an Emergency Operations Center (EOC) providing:
1. Conditions constitute a level of severity that requires employees to work abnormal, extended work hours without a reasonable amount of time to provide for their own meals, or
2. Food or water is not reasonably available for employees to purchase
The meals will be brought to the work location(s) and cost-effective, such as bulk meals.
Not Covered
The following are not covered:
1. Group outings at restaurants or individual meals
2. Meals will not be provided to any employee or volunteer who is receiving a per diem for the same period
title: Update to the Personnel and Safety Rules and Regulations (Disaster Response Meals)

Senate Bill 954, codified as Chapter 2025-182 or Florida Statutes 397.487, requires the adoption of an ordinance establishing application procedures for the owner of a “recovery residence” to request reasonable accommodation from any local land use regulation. Language was added to Section 175-030(F) that allows for the City to impose a cost recovery fee for actual costs incurred by the City to process a reasonable accommodation application based on the fee established and amended by the Resolution of the City Commission.

description: The City is requesting Commission approval to fill a vacant part-time Library Page position at the Richard C. Sullivan Public Library. The position was made vacant when the existing Library Page was promoted to the position of Librarian I. This position performs essential operational functions that support daily library operations and public access during all open hours, including materials check-in and shelving, circulation desk assistance during peak periods, program setup support and collection maintenance. The Library Page also provides critical staffing coverage during lunch breaks, shift transitions and high-use periods. Without this position filled, the library’s ability to maintain consistent two-person coverage during public service hours is impacted, which affects customer service, operational continuity and basic facility oversight. Filling this vacancy is necessary to maintain established service standards, ensure reliable public access and allow professional staff to focus on direct public service responsibilities.

description:
Staff respectfully request City Commission approval to fill the currently vacant part-time IT Systems Analyst position within the Information Technology (IT) Department.
The IT Department is a 3.5-member team responsible for supporting more than 150 City employees across eight municipal facilities throughout the City. This team provides essential technology services that ensure uninterrupted daily operations, system security, and regulatory compliance.
A critical component of this support includes services provided to the Wilton Manors Police Department (WMPD). WMPD operations require specialized technical oversight to maintain compliance with Criminal Justice Information Services (CJIS) standards. These requirements involve secure data management, strict access controls, audit readiness, and immediate response to potential security incidents. Delays or deficiencies in this area could expose the City to significant legal, financial, and operational risks.
In November, the IT Manager position became vacant. The part-time IT Administrator was subsequently promoted to fill that role, resulting in the vacancy of the part-time position, which has since been reclassified as a part-time IT Systems Analyst. Filling this position is critically important to restoring departmental capacity.
Over the past year, the IT Department has undertaken multiple major initiatives to modernize City systems and elevate cybersecurity as a top organizational priority. These capital and infrastructure projects must be balanced with ongoing day-to-day operational support. With current staffing levels, maintaining this balance has become increasingly challenging and unsustainable.
Filling the part-time IT Systems Analyst position will allow the department to continue advancing critical capital projects while maintaining responsive service to City staff. Additionally, this position will be cross-trained to provide backup technical support for WMPD systems. At present, only one team member possesses comprehensive expertise in WMPD’s specialized systems, creating operational vulnerabilities should that individual become unavailable.
As the City continues to grow and adopt new technologies, including cloud-based systems and expanded cybersecurity tools, additional staffing capacity is necessary to prevent service degradation and ensure continued operational resilience. For these reasons, staff respectfully recommend approval to fill the vacant part-time IT Systems Analyst position. Restoring full staffing will stabilize workloads, preserve proactive cybersecurity efforts, reduce operational risk and position the City to effectively manage continued growth and evolving technological demands.
title: Request to Fill Part-Time IT Analyst Position

description:
At the Tuesday, December 10, 2024 Commission Meeting, and in anticipation of outsourcing false alarm reduction management services, the City Commission approved on second reading, Ordinance No. 2024-012 that updated the City's Alarm Systems regulations. False alarms continue to place significant operational strain on the Police Department. Between 2019 and 2025, 73–80% of alarms in Wilton Manors were false, requiring officer deployment to non-emergency events. Each response typically involves two officers performing perimeter checks, interior searches when unsecured entry points are found, and standing by for property owner's arrival. These unnecessary responses divert officers from priority calls and increase personnel expenditures.
The City’s False Alarm Reduction Program previously relied on internal administrative support; however, staffing shortages in the Code Compliance Unit at the time made it impossible to sustain. The program subsequently became dormant, resulting in no structured effort to reduce false alarms.
Subsequent to request for proposal processes, staff determined Alarm Program Systems (APS) offers the strongest solution among the three vendors evaluated. APS will administer, operate, and maintain the City’s False Alarm Reduction Program in compliance with the City’s alarm ordinance, providing all systems, staffing, technology, and support necessary to manage alarm registrations, false alarm tracking, billing, payments, appeals, reporting, and public education. Services include secure data management; integration with the City’s CAD and dispatch systems; account reconciliation and auditing; customer service via mail, phone, email, and web; ordinance compliance support; public awareness initiatives; and proactive identification and mitigation of high-frequency false alarm users, all delivered through a secure, City-branded platform tailored to the City’s operational needs.
Additionally, APS’s revenue-sharing model provides meaningful cost-recovery potential while allowing the City to maintain control of ordinance standards and enforcement. Staff analysis concluded that APS aligns best with Wilton Manors’ expectations regarding service quality, operational efficiency, and financial responsibility. Additional fiscal revenue considerations are shown in the "Fiscal Impacts" section of this report.
The initial contract term is for three (3) years. The City will have the option to extend the term at its sole discretion for two (2), one-year (1-year) renewal terms for a maximum term of five (5) years. This agreement may be terminated by City for convenience, upon thirty (30) days written notice by the City to APS, or by APS, upon six (6) months written notice by APS to the City, in which event APS shall be paid its compensation for services performed to the termination date.

attachments.name: 2026-002 ORD Code Rewrite Chapter - Purchase Water and Wastewater Pass-through Adjustments
Wilton Manors Rate Study Report - Final

description:
The City engaged a professional consultant to conduct a comprehensive utility rates study to evaluate the financial sustainability of the City’s water and wastewater utility systems. As part of that study, the consultant reviewed the City’s reliance on purchased water and wastewater treatment services provided by the City of Fort Lauderdale and identified the need for a formal mechanism to address cost fluctuations outside the City’s direct control.
Historically, increases in purchased water and wastewater treatment costs have required periodic, full rate amendments. The consultant determined that this approach can delay cost recovery and place short-term financial pressure on the utility enterprise funds.
The ordinance implements two distinct pass-through mechanisms recommended in the utility rates study:
Purchased Water Pass-Through Adjustment (PWPTA)
The ordinance authorizes the City to calculate and implement a pass-through adjustment to water rates consistent with the effective date of any change in the cost of purchased water billed by the City of Fort Lauderdale. The City may implement adjustments at any time during the fiscal year when material events occur that impact the financial condition of the water utility system, including but not limited to:
Rate adjustments enacted by the City of Fort Lauderdale;
Unforeseen surcharges or additional billing adjustments; or
Other documented changes in billing for large user water services.
Wastewater Treatment Pass-Through Adjustment (WWTPTA)
Similarly, the ordinance authorizes a pass-through adjustment to wastewater rates based on changes in the cost of purchased wastewater treatment services billed by the City of Fort Lauderdale. Adjustments may be implemented during any portion of the fiscal year due to material events affecting the wastewater utility system, including but not limited to:
Rate adjustments enacted by the City of Fort Lauderdale;
Unforeseen surcharges or additional billing adjustments; or
Other documented changes in wastewater service billing.
These pass-through adjustments are limited in scope to the direct recovery of external cost increases and do not constitute discretionary rate increases. The ordinance provides a clear and predictable framework for aligning City utility rates with actual wholesale service costs, improving fiscal stability while maintaining transparency for utility customers.

description:
Article 090 of the City's Unified Land Development Regulations ("ULDRs") contains the standards for the processing, review, and approval of plats, replats, and amendments to plats within the City of Wilton Manors. The City's review of plats, replats, and amendments to plats includes, but is not limited to, consistency with the City's Comprehensive Plan; the City's ULDRs; street arrangement; adequate drainage; requirements for public buildings and sites; consideration for future development of adjoining land; access; water supply; and sewage disposal. Amendments are proposed to Article 090 of the City's ULDRs to be consistent with updates to Florida Statutes, the BrowardNext - Broward County Land Use Plan, and other updates to include, but not limited to, supplemental application requirements and department/title names. In accordance with Florida Statutes 177.071, the City's approval of plats, replats, and amendments to plats will be administrative. Written notice will be provided to the applicant within seven (7) business days after receipt of the proposed plat, replat, or plat amendment identifying any missing documents or information necessary to process the plat, replat, or plat amendment. In addition, the applicant will be provided with information regarding the plat, replat, or plat amendment approval process and applicable timeframes for reviewing, approving, and processing the plat, replat, or plat amendment application. Changes are also proposed to be consistent with the Countywide platting requirements under Policy 2.13.1 of the BrowardNext - Broward County Land Use Plan. Section 8.11 of the Broward County Charter requires that the Broward County Commission enact an ordinance establishing standards, procedures, and minimum requirements to regulate and control the platting of lands located within Broward County. The Broward County Commission must approve plats of land lying within Broward County prior to recording a plat, replat, or plat amendment in the official records of Broward County, Florida. Broward County requires the municipal approval of all plats, replats, and plat amendments prior to recording. Policy 2.13.1 of the BrowardNext - Broward County Land Use Plan states "no unit of local government may grant an application for a building permit for the construction of a principal building on a parcel of land unless a plat including the parcel or parcels of land has been approved by the Broward County Commission and recorded in the official records of Broward County subsequent to June 4, 1953".
The following changes have been made to the proposed ordinance since the November 10, 2025 Planning and Zoning Board Meeting based on final review by the City Attorney:
• Section 090-030(A)(1) – Add language that states, “The applicant has thirty (30) calendar days to respond to insufficiencies."• Section 090-030(A)(2) – Moved notification language to this section from Section 090-030(A) and renumber remaining sections.
• Section 090-030(A)(4) – Previously Section 090-030(A)(3); add language that requires Community Development Services Director or designee to provide comments within fourteen (14) business days of acceptance of application.
• Section 090-030(A)(5) – Added requirement that approval, approval with conditions or denial must be issued within eight (8) business days upon receiving recommendation from Development Review Committee and clarified article number in ULDRs.
• Section 090-030(C)(1) – Added language that states “The improvement plan must be approved by the Emergency Management/Utility Director or designee in conjunction with site plan approval for the proposed development to be constructed within the boundaries of the plat, replat, or plat amendment."
• Section 090-030(D)(1) – Added language requiring developer’s agreement and invoice for cost recovery of city services performed in conjunction with review of construction improvements.
• Section 090-030(D)(2) – Add section with requirements for approval of developer’s agreement.
• Section 090-030(D)(3) – Add “of the plat, replat, or plat amendment” after recording.
