attachments.name: Request to Fill Vacancy - Code Compliance Officer (FT) (GB146-020326) (2)

description:
Staff respectfully requests City Commission approval to fill the currently vacant full-time Code Compliance Officer position. Staff recommends approval to ensure the City maintains the level of service, responsiveness, and community engagement expected by residents, businesses and visitors as Wilton Manors continues to grow in population, development, and activity.
The Code Compliance Unit is a critical component of the City’s quality-of-life and public safety framework. Operating within the Police Department, the unit is intentionally structured as a service-oriented and community-centered function. Code Compliance Officers work directly with residents, property owners, and businesses to educate, communicate, and achieve voluntary compliance whenever possible. This approach resolves issues more efficiently, reduces escalation, and reinforces the City’s commitment to partnership rather than punitive enforcement.
In recent years, the Code Compliance Unit has operated at or near its maximum sustainable capacity, an achievement we are proud of as it will always be our endeavor to maximize our work product. While staffing levels remained unchanged, the unit absorbed additional responsibilities, including the implementation of the Lien Amnesty Program and the Lien Foreclosure Program, and support for a major records management system migration. These duties are ongoing, and at full staffing we continue facilitating these programs at an acceptable level.
Community feedback underscores the importance of maintaining adequate staffing. While overall satisfaction with Code Compliance services remains mostly positive, survey results reflect a clear expectation for improved presence, responsiveness, and engagement. Filling this vacancy is necessary to improve upon those benchmarks, address resident-identified priorities, and ensure consistent and equitable enforcement across all neighborhoods.
If this vacancy is not filled, we expect overall work output to decrease. Remaining personnel will absorb the vacant position’s workload while continuing to manage expanded program responsibilities. This will impact response times, reduce proactive enforcement efforts, and limit the unit’s ability to engage residents early and often to achieve voluntary compliance, and to coordinate a collective effort to present a case before the Special Magistrate. We must refuse to become an “enforcement machine” absent community engagement as our City takes pride in providing a professional, responsive and personable level of service to ensure "Life Continues to be Better Here"!
If this vacancy is not filled, our operations will shift toward a more reactive, complaint-driven model, reducing the unit’s ability to function as a visible, approachable, and problem-solving resource within the community. This outcome is inconsistent with the City’s established compliance philosophy and long-term quality of life goals.
For these reasons, staff respectfully recommends City Commission approval to fill the vacant Code Compliance Officer position. Restoring full staffing through your support will stabilize workloads, prevent reductions in output, preserve proactive and community focused service delivery, and ensure the City is well-positioned to manage continued growth and future program responsibilities.
title: Request to fill full-time Code Compliance Officer vacancy.

description:
The position of Assistant Finance Director was recently vacated, and we are requesting approval to fill it. The Assistant Finance Director is a mission-critical leadership role within the Finance Department and is essential to maintaining the City’s fiscal integrity, operational continuity, regulatory compliance, and strategic financial planning.
Operational NecessityThe Assistant Finance Director oversees core financial functions, including financial reporting, audit coordination, internal controls, compliance with state and federal regulations, and supervision of key finance personnel. These duties cannot be deferred or absorbed indefinitely without risk. The absence of this position places significant strain on departmental capacity and concentrates critical responsibilities, increasing institutional risk.
Financial Stewardship and OversightMaintaining strong internal controls and accurate financial reporting is fundamental to protecting public funds and ensuring transparency. This role directly supports preparation of the Annual Comprehensive Financial Report, coordination of external audits, grant compliance, debt management, and budget monitoring. Delays or gaps in these areas could expose the City to audit findings, compliance issues, or diminished financial credibility.
Organizational Continuity and Risk MitigationThe Assistant Finance Director serves as the department’s second-in-command and is essential for continuity of operations, particularly during emergencies, audits, budget season, or unplanned absences. Without this position filled, the City lacks adequate redundancy in financial leadership, which is inconsistent with best practices in municipal governance and risk management.
Fiscal ResponsibilityThis position is already included and fully funded in the current fiscal year budget; therefore, filling the vacancy is cost-neutral and does not require any additional appropriation or budget amendment. Leaving the role vacant does not produce meaningful long-term cost savings. Instead, it may result in inefficiencies, increased overtime, delayed projects, and potential external consulting costs that exceed any temporary salary savings. Filling the position ensures work is performed internally, efficiently, and under appropriate professional oversight.
ConclusionThe Finance Department plays a central role in supporting every City operation, and the Assistant Finance Director position is indispensable to maintaining that support at the level expected by the Commission and the public. Filling this vacancy is not an expansion of staff, but the restoration of a previously authorized and budgeted position necessary for the City’s financial stability and operational effectiveness. For these reasons, we respectfully request approval to proceed with recruitment and hiring for the Assistant Finance Director position.

MASTER Lien Foreclosure Case File - 1424 NE 23 Street #1-2 (GB146-102025)

description:
Code Case No. 21-000479 was opened on March 17, 2021 for multiple violations of the City’s Code of Ordinances at the subject property. An Order Imposing Fine and Lien was entered by the Special Magistrate on September 1, 2021. The property was sold to the current owner, Vincent Vigliotti, on March 17, 2022. The City’s code enforcement lien, however, was not recorded until May 10, 2022, after the ownership transfer occurred. Following review, legal counsel advised that foreclosure should not be pursued because the lien was recorded after the current owner acquired the property, and therefore the owner did not have notice of the lien at the time of purchase. Florida Statute §162.06(5) requires a transferring owner to disclose pending code enforcement proceedings to a prospective purchaser and provides protections to new owners when such disclosures are not made. Based on the timing of the lien recording and statutory requirements, legal counsel concluded that foreclosure action would not be legally appropriate in this case. As a result, staff is bringing this matter before the Commission to request authorization to release the lien in accordance with legal guidance. The value of the lien as of January 8, 2026 was $418,750.00.
WMPD Policy #600 - Code Compliance Unit instructs staff to record liens with the Broward County Clerk of Courts within 72 hours of the Magistrate certifying an Order Imposing Fine and Lien. This standard was not met, and corrective action has been taken. A new code case (25-000570) was opened under the current owner for property maintenance related violations, and a recorded lien continues to accrue due to non-compliance.
title: Request for the Commission to release a code enforcement lien attached to the real property located at 1424 – 1428 NE 23 Street #1-2, Wilton Manors, Florida 33305, associated with Code Case No. 21-000479, pursuant to legal review and recommendation.

attachments.name: 2026-002 ORD Code Rewrite Chapter - Purchase Water and Wastewater Pass-through Adjustments
Wilton Manors Rate Study Report - Final

description:
The City engaged a professional consultant to conduct a comprehensive utility rates study to evaluate the financial sustainability of the City’s water and wastewater utility systems. As part of that study, the consultant reviewed the City’s reliance on purchased water and wastewater treatment services provided by the City of Fort Lauderdale and identified the need for a formal mechanism to address cost fluctuations outside the City’s direct control.
Historically, increases in purchased water and wastewater treatment costs have required periodic, full rate amendments. The consultant determined that this approach can delay cost recovery and place short-term financial pressure on the utility enterprise funds.
The ordinance implements two distinct pass-through mechanisms recommended in the utility rates study:
Purchased Water Pass-Through Adjustment (PWPTA)
The ordinance authorizes the City to calculate and implement a pass-through adjustment to water rates consistent with the effective date of any change in the cost of purchased water billed by the City of Fort Lauderdale. The City may implement adjustments at any time during the fiscal year when material events occur that impact the financial condition of the water utility system, including but not limited to:
Rate adjustments enacted by the City of Fort Lauderdale;
Unforeseen surcharges or additional billing adjustments; or
Other documented changes in billing for large user water services.
Wastewater Treatment Pass-Through Adjustment (WWTPTA)
Similarly, the ordinance authorizes a pass-through adjustment to wastewater rates based on changes in the cost of purchased wastewater treatment services billed by the City of Fort Lauderdale. Adjustments may be implemented during any portion of the fiscal year due to material events affecting the wastewater utility system, including but not limited to:
Rate adjustments enacted by the City of Fort Lauderdale;
Unforeseen surcharges or additional billing adjustments; or
Other documented changes in wastewater service billing.
These pass-through adjustments are limited in scope to the direct recovery of external cost increases and do not constitute discretionary rate increases. The ordinance provides a clear and predictable framework for aligning City utility rates with actual wholesale service costs, improving fiscal stability while maintaining transparency for utility customers.

description:
Article 090 of the City's Unified Land Development Regulations ("ULDRs") contains the standards for the processing, review, and approval of plats, replats, and amendments to plats within the City of Wilton Manors. The City's review of plats, replats, and amendments to plats includes, but is not limited to, consistency with the City's Comprehensive Plan; the City's ULDRs; street arrangement; adequate drainage; requirements for public buildings and sites; consideration for future development of adjoining land; access; water supply; and sewage disposal. Amendments are proposed to Article 090 of the City's ULDRs to be consistent with updates to Florida Statutes, the BrowardNext - Broward County Land Use Plan, and other updates to include, but not limited to, supplemental application requirements and department/title names. In accordance with Florida Statutes 177.071, the City's approval of plats, replats, and amendments to plats will be administrative. Written notice will be provided to the applicant within seven (7) business days after receipt of the proposed plat, replat, or plat amendment identifying any missing documents or information necessary to process the plat, replat, or plat amendment. In addition, the applicant will be provided with information regarding the plat, replat, or plat amendment approval process and applicable timeframes for reviewing, approving, and processing the plat, replat, or plat amendment application. Changes are also proposed to be consistent with the Countywide platting requirements under Policy 2.13.1 of the BrowardNext - Broward County Land Use Plan. Section 8.11 of the Broward County Charter requires that the Broward County Commission enact an ordinance establishing standards, procedures, and minimum requirements to regulate and control the platting of lands located within Broward County. The Broward County Commission must approve plats of land lying within Broward County prior to recording a plat, replat, or plat amendment in the official records of Broward County, Florida. Broward County requires the municipal approval of all plats, replats, and plat amendments prior to recording. Policy 2.13.1 of the BrowardNext - Broward County Land Use Plan states "no unit of local government may grant an application for a building permit for the construction of a principal building on a parcel of land unless a plat including the parcel or parcels of land has been approved by the Broward County Commission and recorded in the official records of Broward County subsequent to June 4, 1953".
The following changes have been made to the proposed ordinance since the November 10, 2025 Planning and Zoning Board Meeting based on final review by the City Attorney:
• Section 090-030(A)(1) – Add language that states, “The applicant has thirty (30) calendar days to respond to insufficiencies."• Section 090-030(A)(2) – Moved notification language to this section from Section 090-030(A) and renumber remaining sections.
• Section 090-030(A)(4) – Previously Section 090-030(A)(3); add language that requires Community Development Services Director or designee to provide comments within fourteen (14) business days of acceptance of application.
• Section 090-030(A)(5) – Added requirement that approval, approval with conditions or denial must be issued within eight (8) business days upon receiving recommendation from Development Review Committee and clarified article number in ULDRs.
• Section 090-030(C)(1) – Added language that states “The improvement plan must be approved by the Emergency Management/Utility Director or designee in conjunction with site plan approval for the proposed development to be constructed within the boundaries of the plat, replat, or plat amendment."
• Section 090-030(D)(1) – Added language requiring developer’s agreement and invoice for cost recovery of city services performed in conjunction with review of construction improvements.
• Section 090-030(D)(2) – Add section with requirements for approval of developer’s agreement.
• Section 090-030(D)(3) – Add “of the plat, replat, or plat amendment” after recording.

description:
The City’s anticipated allocation of Community Block Grant dollars for the 52nd year funding cycle (2026/2027) is estimated at $76,000. The primary objective of CDBG funds is to assist low to moderate income persons or neighborhoods to improve their quality of life. This may be achieved by developing social programs or through infrastructure improvements. According to the socio-economic data collected by the county, the eligible neighborhoods in Wilton Manors for capital or infrastructure improvements are in the southwest and south central areas in the City.
CDBG funds have been utilized in the past to re-build the sewage lift station, construct sidewalks and a drainage system, and resurface streets in the Highland Estates neighborhood. Funds have also been utilized to improve Stafford Park , including the construction or installation of estate style fencing, an emergency generator, a 35-foot floating dock, an addition to the community center building, an artificial turf surface on the playground, a shade structure on the rear deck, fitness station, a shade structure over the fitness station, a basketball court renovation, and security cameras. Funds have also been utilized to acquire and develop the property adjacent to Stafford Park at 811 N.E. 28th Street. More recently, funds were allocated for improvements to the existing ball field and a new storage and maintenance facility building at Mickel Park and drainage improvements on the west side of the City. The first phase of energy efficient lighting installations at Hagen Park was recently completed.
Broward County has advised that no new social service programs, such as possible computer training, will be funded with CDBG funds. This is due to the limitation by HUD regulations that such programs may not exceed fifteen percent of the total allocations to all cities through the county. Existing programs already meet that maximum allowed level and, in fact, due to the substantial reduction in funding to all the cities, some existing social service programs have had to be cut back to stay within the fifteen percent cap.
This public hearing provides an opportunity to receive input from residents. This is the first public meeting being held for the 52nd Year CDBG program. At the conclusion of the second public meeting, held at a future Commission meeting, City Staff will present a project for Commission approval based on the public input and the parameters of the grant application.

description:
The City’s master Lift Station #11 (LS-11) utilizes three (3) pumps to send wastewater to the G.T. Lohmeyer Wastewater Treatment Plant within the City of Fort Lauderdale. The pumping arrangement operates on an automatic rotating basis among these pumps, typically with only one or two pumps operating at any given time. All pumps may be in operation at a single time, but this only occurs during times of extreme flow. A recent on-site inspection by Xylem Water Solutions USA, Inc. (Xylem), the pump manufacturer, revealed Pumps #1 and #2 have excessive wear and require further detailed inspection. Pump #3 was replaced in 2024 and is in good condition.
Pump #2 was removed from service, and a detailed shop-inspection determined a complete re-build would be required at a cost of $100,786.82, with a 6 to 8-week lead time. Upon inquiry, a new replacement pump would cost $107,710.00, however, the lead time is up to 28 weeks. Staff determined that Pump #2 should be rebuilt to expedite its reinstallation. Considering that Pump #1 likely requires a similar re-build, staff recommend purchasing a new pump, which would drastically cut the lead time to have all three pumps back in full operation. LS-11 operates with Flygt-brand pumps as the standard for the station. Xylem Water Solutions USA, Inc. is the manufacturer of this proprietary brand and is therefore the only source for repair and replacement.
title: Motion to approve the purchase of one (1) new replacement wastewater pump for Lift Station #11.

description:
The FY25-26 budget includes an allocation of $40,000 to conduct a comprehensive Classification and Compensation Study. These studies are essential and typically conducted every two to four years to ensure the City maintains parity with comparable municipalities in terms of pay structures and compensation practices. Regular reviews help ensure that employees are compensated fairly for the work they perform, support the City’s ability to recruit highly qualified candidates and strengthen efforts to retain existing talent. Maintaining a competitive compensation structure is critical to sustaining a high-performing workforce and delivering quality services to the community.
We recommend contracting with HR Compensation Consultants (HRCC) to perform the study. HRCC has extensive experience working with public-sector organizations and provides a comprehensive scope of work that includes classification reviews, market analysis, pay structure evaluation and implementation recommendations. As part of the market analysis, HRCC will collect pay range data from 12 public-sector organizations for up to 40 key benchmark positions. These organizations include Broward County, Fort Lauderdale, Oakland Park, Coral Springs, Coconut Creek, Parkland and others selected to provide a representative and competitive market comparison. The projected cost for HRCC to conduct the study is $30,000, which is within the adopted budget. The anticipated timeline for completion is four months, beginning at project kickoff and concluding with a presentation of findings and recommendations to the City Commission.
Approval of this item will authorize the City to engage HRCC and initiate the Classification and Compensation Study for FY25-26.
title: Motion to Approve Classification & Compensation Study by HR Compensation Consultants, LLC

description:
Background:The Wilton Manors Police Department (WMPD) currently relies heavily on personal mobile devices for official communication and access to work-related systems. Many staff members use their personal phones for calls, emails, and applications that involve sensitive or confidential information. This practice raises significant data security and privacy concerns and presents potential noncompliance issues with Criminal Justice Information Services (CJIS) requirements.
Discussion:To address these concerns and improve operational efficiency, WMPD is proposing the implementation of department-issued Apple iPhones for staff members. These devices will be managed under a Mobile Device Management (MDM) platform, ensuring compliance with CJIS standards, remote security management, and centralized software and application updates.
Through the MDM platform, the City can maintain strict control over data access, enforce security protocols, and remotely lock or wipe devices if they are lost or compromised. This level of oversight will enhance the Department’s ability to protect sensitive information while improving communication capabilities and accountability.
The iPhones will provide secure and convenient access to key tools including City email, Microsoft Teams, Axon, and other approved law enforcement applications. By standardizing mobile devices, WMPD will strengthen its technology infrastructure and align with best practices in secure law enforcement communication and data management.

description:
The City's employee benefits consultant and City staff solicit competitive bids for employee health and wellness benefits on an annual basis. For the 2026 renewal year, the City received health insurance proposals from three providers: Florida Blue, Cigna, and Aetna. The City is not considering Aetna due to recent changes in their network and significant differences in their coverage levels, which are not comparable to what employees currently receive. The City received an initial renewal proposal from its current provider, Florida Blue, reflecting an 18.4% increase in premiums. This was successfully negotiated down to an 8.25% increase over current rates. Cigna also submitted a competitive proposal, which is 7.00% above current premiums. Cigna’s Qualified High Deductible Health Plan (QHDHP) would offer benefits very similar to the City’s current plan with Florida Blue. However, two concerns make transitioning to Cigna undesirable at this time:In 2024, the City transitioned from United Healthcare (UHC) to Florida Blue. Switching again, after only one year, to Cigna may negatively impact the City’s ability to secure competitive bids for the 2027 plan year and could result in higher premiums.
A major current concern is that Florida Blue is not in-network with Memorial and Broward Health. It is reasonably likely that Florida Blue will renegotiate its contract and return to in-network status with Memorial and Broward Health by the end of the current calendar year. If the City were to switch to Cigna and Cigna subsequently fails to renew its contracts, employees could again face limited access to key healthcare providers. The insurance committee unanimously voted to renew with Florida Blue with the expectation of a new agreement between them and both Broward and Memorial Health, bringing Florida Blue back in-network. If an agreement fails to materialize, the consensus from the insurance committee was to rebid the plan in early 2026 to ensure employees have a health plan with all the local hospitals in-network.
The City will continue using Optum Bank for employee HSAs. It has negotiated a 4% premium increase with its current dental insurance provider, Ameritas. Life insurance and long-term disability (LTD) coverage will remain with Mutual of Omaha, with no change in premiums. The combined increase in dental and health insurance premiums, along with no change to life and LTD coverage, results in an overall increase of 6.9%. The FY 2025–2026 budget had allocated funds for a 20.00% increase in premiums. For context, the 10-year average increase in health insurance premiums is 3.26%.
title: Presentation by Maureen Pentland of EBS Advisors, Inc. and Motion to Approve 2026 City Insurance Renewal Options

description:
The City is required by Federal and State regulations to provide monthly bacteriological and quarterly disinfectant by-products sampling and testing for drinking water distributed through the City’s water supply system. Sampling entails labor to collect samples, laboratory testing, and providing written reports of sampling results. While the City purchases its water from the City of Fort Lauderdale, the City is responsible for providing the required sampling. The City also provides sampling for occasional resident requests.

attachments.name: Xylem - LS-11 Rehab pump #1 - Sole Source

description:
The City’s master Lift Station #11 (LS-11) utilizes three (3) pumps to send wastewater to the G.T. Lohmeyer Wastewater Treatment Plant within the City of Fort Lauderdale. The pumping arrangement operates on an automatic rotating basis among these pumps, typically with only one or two pumps operating at any given time. All pumps may be in operation at a single time, but this only occurs during times of extreme flow. A recent on-site inspection by Xylem Water Solutions USA, Inc. (Xylem), the pump manufacturer, revealed Pumps #1 and #2 have excessive wear and require further detailed inspection. Pump #3 was replaced in 2024 and is in good condition.
Pump #2 was removed from service, and a detailed shop-inspection determined a complete re-build would be required at a cost of $100,786.82, with a 6 to 8-week lead time. Upon inquiry, a new replacement pump would cost $107,710.00, however, the lead time is up to 28 weeks. Staff determined that Pump #2 should be rebuilt to expedite its reinstallation. Considering that Pump #1 likely requires a similar re-build, staff recommend purchasing a new pump, which would drastically cut the lead time to have all three pumps back in full operation. LS-11 operates with Flygt-brand pumps as the standard for the station. Xylem Water Solutions USA, Inc. is the manufacturer of this proprietary brand and is therefore the only source for repair and replacement.
title: Motion to approve the purchase of one (1) new replacement wastewater pump for Lift Station #11.

description:
The Police Department seeks Commission approval for the purchase of six (6) 2025 Police Interceptor SUVs for a total of $274,116.00. These vehicles will be assigned to the patrol division and will replace six (6) police pursuit-rated vehicles that have reached, or are anticipated to reach, the end of their useful lifespan.
To determine which vehicles will be replaced, evaluations will be made by department staff and/or the City’s contracted subject matter expert(s) to assess vehicle age and model year, mileage, crash history, mechanical condition and general appearance. Additional factors considered will be total engine and idle hours, which are indicators of actual vehicle wear due to extensive idling typical of law enforcement operations. Other considerations include duty cycle intensity, overall maintenance and repair history, and the compatibility of existing in-car technology with updated operational requirements.
Projected model years to be replaced are 2015 - 2017. This purchase complies with the City's current vehicle capital replacement plan and includes a 3-year/36,000-mile bumper-to-bumper warranty and a 5-year/100,000-mile powertrain warranty for all vehicles. Attachments reflect detailed quotations and supporting materials from Duval Ford.
If approved, the Police Department will proceed with the immediate purchase of six (6) 2025 model Ford SUV Interceptors from Duval Ford, LLC that are readily available for purchase and delivery. Securing the 2025 models will help ensure the vehicles will be outfitted and ready for service by early spring 2026, while 2026 models would delay delivery and deployment well into summer or fall 2026. Given our aging fleet, vehicles are needed as soon as possible.
All vehicles if approved for purchase will be procured under the Florida Sheriffs Association (FSA) Cooperative Purchasing Program, Contract FSA25-VEL33.0: Pursuit, Administrative, and Other Vehicles. The statewide contract, effective October 1, 2025, through September 30, 2027, ensures compliance with all FSA contractual terms and conditions. Duval Ford LLC is one of the 32 authorized vendors awarded under this cooperative agreement.
title: Motion to approve the purchase of six (6) police pursuit rated vehicles for the Police Department.

attachments.name: Heights Proposed by CGA Prior to the Adoption of Current HUB Map (1)

description:
On August 24, 2021, the City Commission adopted Ordinance No. 2021-011 which included the absolute maximum height for the Urban Center Mixed Use Zoning Districts. Section 030-038 of the City's Unified Land Development Regulations (“ULDRs”) provides the absolute maximum height (allowable base height plus additional incentive height) within the Urban Center Mixed Use Zoning Districts.
During the February 11, 2025 City Commission meeting, the City Manager requested clarification of topics for an upcoming workshop based on a re-evaluation of Article 030 of the City's ULDRs consistent with the City’s Strategic Plan goals to promote economic development, enhance quality of life, and livability. Those topics include the evaluation of maximum height; rezoning of Transit Oriented Corridor West (TOC-W) to bifurcate parcels adjacent to Andrews Avenue from the parcels adjacent to Oakland Park Boulevard and the creation of a new zoning district; rezoning of parcels adjacent to Colohatchee Park to Transit Oriented Corridor East (TOC-E); an evaluation of dimensional requirements and the required number of parking spaces; consideration of additional types of parking spaces; setbacks; the minimum square footage of a dwelling unit; and rental conversions as it relates to height incentives for affordable housing.
At the March 11, 2025, City Commission Meeting, City staff was directed to schedule one (1) Article 030 re-evaluation item at a time for discussion in lieu of scheduling a City Commission workshop.
On April 27, 2021, a HUB Map workshop was held to discuss potential height for the Urban Center Mixed Use Districts prior to the approval of Ordinance No. 2021-011 which adopted the HUB Map. A copy of the heights proposed by Calvin Giordano and Associates is attached for your reference. The height discussion was heard at the April 22, 2025, City Commission meeting. The City Commission directed staff to provide suggested changes to height within the Urban Center Mixed Use Districts with a focus on Andrews Avenue based on input from the public, previous height suggestions by Calvin Giordano and Associates, and input from developers. A Developer's Summit was held at Hagen Park on September 17, 2025. Comments from developers, financiers, and land use attorneys included, but not limited to, suggested increases in height and density. The Community Development Services Department held three (3) open houses to obtain input on suggested changes to permitted heights within the Urban Center Mixed Use Districts on September 22, 2025. Comments from open house attendees included, but not limited to: supportive of additional height on NE 24 Street; retention of existing setbacks with more height and density; protection of quality of life; supportive of ten (10) stories like Wilton Tower; the larger the parcel, the more height; and maintenance of existing height for areas proposed to be rezoned to Transit Oriented Corridor East (TOC-E).
Staff is seeking direction from the City Commission relating to the proposed changes to the HUB Height Map.
title: Discussion of Article 30 HUB Height Map

attachments.name: 2025-082 RESO Approving ILA with FLL For Fire Rescue (2025-2030)
ILA with FLL for Fire Rescue (2025-2030)

description:
The City of Fort Lauderdale has provided professional fire protection and emergency medical services (EMS) to the City of Wilton Manors since June 2000 under a long-standing interlocal partnership. Over the past 25 years, this partnership has ensured high-quality emergency response, advanced life support capabilities, and access to specialized fire-rescue resources.
The current agreement, executed in 2015, and its subsequent amendments have consistently delivered effective and reliable service to Wilton Manors residents and businesses. The first amendment to the 2015 ILA expired on September 30, 2025, and was temporarily extended through October 31, 2025, to allow both parties sufficient time to negotiate a new five-year agreement that reflects evolving service demands, cost structures, and operational improvements.
City staff, in coordination with the Fort Lauderdale Fire Rescue Department and legal counsel, have completed negotiations on a new five-year Interlocal Agreement (ILA) to continue these vital public safety services for the period November 1, 2025, through October 31, 2030.
The proposed five-year ILA maintains continuity of fire and EMS services to the residents and businesses of Wilton Manors while incorporating several key updates and financial provisions reflective of current operational needs and cost structures.
Highlights of the new agreement include:
Contract Cost:Annual cost of $4,758,814, representing a 14.6% increase ($606,596) over the prior year.
The increase is primarily attributed to rising personnel costs (as the City of Fort Lauderdale is currently in the midst of collective bargaining negotiations), higher insurance costs, investment in new IT hardware and software licenses, and general inflationary pressures affecting equipment, supplies, and operational costs.
Staffing Enhancement:Addition of one (1) personnel to the Advanced Life Support (ALS) Rescue/Transport Unit for the duration of the Staffing for Adequate Fire and Emergency Response (SAFER) Grant period.
Upon the expiration of the SAFER Grant, the City of Wilton Manors will contribute to the costs associated with the additional firefighter using the same cost allocation methodology applied under this agreement.
Other highlights:Future contract costs will increase by no more than 10% in any given year.
The City of Wilton Manors will retain ownership of Fire Engine 16.
The City of Wilton Manors will contribute towards the replacement of the Rescue Unit vehicle and, in doing so, will gain an ownership stake in that apparatus.
Wilton Manors’ vehicle replacement contributions will continue to accrue in an interest-bearing account maintained by Fort Lauderdale.
The City of Fort Lauderdale shall not assert any right or claim to the Chapter 175 insurance premium tax revenues used to finance the Wilton Manors Volunteer Firefighters Retirement System.

attachments.name: 2025-081 RESO Appointing Seven Members to Public Art Board (PAB)

description: The City Commission will vote on the individuals to be appointed to this board.The Public Art Board (PAB) is an advisory board appointed by the City Commission, consisting of seven (7) members. The board is structured to include three arts professionals and two City residents with a strong interest and knowledge of visual arts. The remaining two members may either be arts professionals or City residents. Arts professionals must either own an art-related business within the City or be professionally involved in the Wilton Manors arts community, though they are not required to be residents of the City. The PAB plays a critical role in reviewing artists’ credentials and conceptual design proposals, providing recommendations to ensure that public art projects align with the City’s cultural and aesthetic vision.

attachments.name: 2025-069 RESO Amended and Restated Master Utility Resolution-Wilton Manors(888702.4)

description:
On December 13, 2022, the City Commission gave the City Manager consent to prepare and submit the required Letter of Interest (LOI) to begin the debt financing through the Water Infrastructure Finance and Innovation Act (WIFIA), a federal program overseen by the Environmental Protection Agency (EPA). The WIFIA program provides long-term, low-interest federal loans for eligible water infrastructure projects. This financing will enable the City to advance critical projects identified in the Water, Wastewater, and Stormwater Integrated Master Plan, enhancing system capacity, reliability, and resiliency.
Following submission of the LOI and subsequent application, the EPA has invited the City to move forward in the WIFIA loan process. To proceed, the City Commission must adopt a Master Resolution and related Supplemental Resolutions authorizing the issuance of debt and the execution of all documents required under the WIFIA loan program.
Adoption of the Master Resolution establishes the framework for the City to enter into one or more WIFIA loan agreements, subject to Commission approval of individual supplemental resolutions.

description:
The FY25-26 budget proposes an ad valorem operating millage rate of 6.2270 mills. This millage rate represents a decrease of 3% over the current fiscal year’s millage rate and an increase of 4.11% over the rolled-back millage rate of 5.9809. The city's taxable value increased by 7.70% as of July 1, 2025.
The voted debt service millage rate for the 2008 City Hall Bond Debt has decreased from 0.1782 in Fiscal Year 2024-25 to 0.1661 in Fiscal Year 2025-26, a reduction of 0.0121 mills (6.8%).
The overall city-wide millage rate, combining the operating and debt service rates, is 6.3931, a decrease of (0.2047) or (3.1%) over the FY24-25 combined millage rate of 6.5978.
The City's total budgeted ad valorem revenues for Fiscal Year 2025-26, as adjusted by the expected collection rate, are $15,262,830. This represents an increase of $580,544 in overall budgeted ad valorem revenues over FY24-25.
The fiscal impact on the average single-family home taxpayer with homestead exemptions under the Save Our Homes amendment is a decrease of $6 annually.

description:
The "Wilton Manors Townhomes" plat was approved by the City Commission on June 10, 2025 for fifty (50) townhouse units for the property located at 1550 NE 26 Street with Folio Numbers 494226000536 and 494226000531. The plat includes fifty (50) individual townhouse lots, two (2) recreation tracts, two (2) right of way tracts, and a Parcel A that includes common area, drainage/retention area, and internal private roads. The subject parcel is located at the southeast corner of NE 15 Avenue and NE 26 Street. The parcel currently contains a parking lot that was formerly accessory to a house of worship that was demolished in 2022.
The applicant requests to allow for building permits to be issued for the project prior to the plat being recorded to include, but not limited to, retaining wall, site work, and buildings. Per Section 090-010(A)(4) of the City's Unified Land Development Regulations, a building permit may be issued for a parcel of land for which a plat approval has been given by the Broward County Board of County Commissioners although the plat has not yet been recorded, provided such authorization is granted in an agreement among the developer, the City and the County. The developer's agreement shall at a minimum require compliance with the applicable provisions of plat approval and shall prohibit the issuance of a certificate of occupancy until the plat is recorded. The City and Broward County shall be required to make a finding that facilities and services will be available at the adopted level of service standards concurrent with the issuance of the building permit(s).

description:
In January 2019, the City of Wilton Manors selected Baxter & Woodman, Inc. to prepare a comprehensive Water, Wastewater & Stormwater Integrated Master Plan (IMP). This plan, completed in January 2020, provides a detailed inventory and analysis of the City’s existing utility infrastructure, along with strategic recommendations for maintenance, repair, and replacement over a 25-year period. A key component of the IMP is the Capital Improvement Plan (CIP) which outlines a total of fifty-four (54) projects: seventeen (17) for water distribution, sixteen for (16) wastewater, and twenty-one (21) for stormwater management. These projects are prioritized over two (2) planning horizons - short-term (1 to 10 years) and long-term (11 to 25 years and beyond).
Since the IMP’s completion five years ago, the City has made progress implementing several of the recommended projects. However, changes in projected growth, development trends, and environmental factors have influenced system demands and long-term infrastructure needs. As a result, the City will undertake an update of the CIP to reassess and reprioritize the remaining projects based on current goals, anticipated growth, and budgetary considerations. The updated CIP will continue to categorize projects within the original planning horizons and service as a formal supplement to the original IMP.
The City’s consultant, Baxter & Woodman, Inc. (B&W) has proposed to provide overall project management, data collection, and analysis of the water distribution system, wastewater system, and stormwater systems to provide an update of the CIP for a cost of $53,470.00 per their proposal dated June 16, 2025.

description:
Since 2015, the City of Wilton Manors has used Vermont Systems’ software suite as the foundation of its Parks and Recreation operations. The suite includes:
RecTrac: the internal recreation management system used by staff for activity registration, facility rentals, membership/pass sales, financial reporting, and POS transactions.
WebTrac: the public-facing resident portal allowing 24/7 online program registration, account management, and facility booking.
PayTrac: the integrated, PCI-compliant payment platform used for secure credit card and ACH transactions both online and in-person.
These systems are fully embedded in both resident-facing services and internal operational workflows. The software integrates with the City’s financial systems, supports ongoing public engagement, and serves as the revenue and registration backbone for Leisure Services.
Vermont Systems, Inc. is the sole developer, licensor, and service provider for RecTrac, WebTrac, and PayTrac. There are no third-party resellers or support vendors. The company has provided documentation confirming its sole source status.
Designating these tools as a City Standard Commodity will allow the City to avoid a disruptive procurement or system replacement process and maintain uninterrupted service delivery. To support this designation and provide stability in service delivery, staff recommend entering into a five-year agreement with Vermont Systems, Inc. for hosting, support, and payment processing services. The new agreement would take effect October 1, 2025 and extend through September 30, 2030.
This request aligns with Section II.B.4 of the City’s Purchasing Policy and Procedures Manual, which allows designation of City Standard Commodities where only one vendor or product is suitable for operational performance and compatibility.
A full justification packet from Vermont Systems is included with this item, along with a signed City Standard/Sole Source form and current quote.

description:
Spartacus NightClubs LLC, doing business as Eagle Wilton Manors, located at 2209 Wilton Drive, has submitted a Specific Use Permit Application, requesting an extension of the hours to serve and sell alcoholic beverages in accordance with Section 3-9(f) of the City of Wilton Manors ("City") Code of Ordinances ("Code"). Section 3-9(f) of the City’s Code governs the hours during which alcoholic beverages may be sold, served, or delivered and process for requesting an extension of these hours. No person, vendor, or employee of a state-licensed vendor may sell, offer for sale, deliver, or serve any liquor, beer, or wine regardless of alcohol contact on Monday through Friday between the hours of 2:00 a.m. and 7:00 a.m., and on Saturday and Sunday between the hours of 3:00 a.m. and 7:00 a.m. Section 3-9(f) states that the request and/or approval of an exemption shall not exceed past 4:00 a.m. The extended hours requested by Eagle Wilton Manors are as follows:Sunday, August 31, 2025, from 3:00 a.m. to 4:00 a.m.
Saturday, November 29, 2025, from 3:00 a.m. to 4:00 a.m.
Thursday, January 1, 2026, from 2:00 a.m. to 4:00 a.m.
Sunday, February 15, 2026, from 2:00 a.m. to 4:00 a.m.
Sunday, May 24, 2026, from 2:00 a.m. to 4:00 a.m.
City staff have reviewed the request to ensure consistency with Section 3-9(f) of the City's Code, which includes, but is not limited to, the City of Wilton Manor's Comprehensive Plan, the City's Unified Land Development Regulations, impacts on traffic circulation, impacts on pedestrian safety, nuisance factors, screening and buffering of adjacent property, neighborhood scale and character, and whether off-duty sworn officers are required.
City staff is recommending approval of the extension request for the following dates with the condition that the sale and service of alcoholic beverages and the consumption of these alcoholic beverages are limited to the inside of the bar (bricks and mortar), with no outside sale, service or consumption and off-duty detail officers are required as outlined in the August 18, 2025, memorandum from Chief Blocker.
Thursday, January 1, 2026, from 2:00 a.m. to 4:00 a.m.
Sunday, February 15, 2026, from 3:00 a.m. to 4:00 a.m.
Sunday, May 24, 2026, from 3:00 a.m. to 4:00 a.m.

description:
The proposed text amendment to the City of Wilton Manors Comprehensive Plan to allow for double density for hotel and Special Residential Facility Category (3) units and the addition of a Property Rights Element are consistent with the goals, objectives, and policies of the City’s Comprehensive Plan to encourage redevelopment and revitalization. The proposed text amendment to allow for double density for hotel units and Special Residential Category Facility (3) development will utilize residential dwelling units that are currently allowed by the City of Wilton Manors Land Use Plan within the Transit Oriented Corridor (TOC), Transit Oriented Corridor West (TOC-West), Low (5) Residential, Low-Medium (10) Residential, and Medium-High (25) Residential land use designations. In addition, available flexibility and redevelopment units permissible by the Broward County Land Use Plan are also available. Level of service standards are satisfied for all previously approved land use designations currently permitted through the City’s land use plan. In addition, through the City’s development approval process, each proposed project utilizing double density will be evaluated to ensure that all the City’s level of service standards are met, which include potable water, sanitary sewer, drainage, solid waste, traffic, public education, and parks.
On June 28, 2021, the Governor signed into law an amendment to Florida Statue 163.3177 to implement the requirements of House Bill 59. This amendment requires local governments to adopt and include a Property Rights Element in its comprehensive plan for any proposed plan amendment initiated after July 1, 2021. Florida Statutes 163.3177(6)(i) requires that local governments ensure that judicially acknowledged and constitutionally protected private property rights continue to be respected and considered in local decision-making. The proposed Property Rights Element is consistent with the requirements of Florida Statute 163.3177.

description:
Code Case #23-003752: The owner of the property located at 2101 N Dixie Hwy at the time of the violation, Rosalind Perlmutter was sent the first Notice of Violation on December 26, 2023, for Building Safety Inspection Program – Obtain permits for 25 year building safety inspection program, requesting compliance within thirty (30) days, or the case would be brought to the Special Magistrate. The property was not brought into compliance, and the Special Magistrate Hearing was set for March 6, 2024.
On March 6, 2024, the Special Magistrate heard this case and affirmed the violation, giving the property owner until May 5, 2024 to achieve compliance or face a fine of $250.00 per day plus a $200.00 administrative fee (which was paid). Routine inspections were completed on this property seeking voluntary compliance with negative results. Failure to achieve compliance within the required time prompted the case to be scheduled for the July 10, 2024, Special Magistrate Hearing to impose the fine and lien on the property.
On July 10, 2024, the Special Magistrate rendered an Order Certifying and Imposing Fine and Lien on the property.
On March 4, 2025, the property was brought into compliance. By that time, the property had remained in violation for a total of 303 days, resulting in a $75,750.00 lien.
On July 2, 2025, the Special Magistrate reduced the fine 50% to $37,875.00 which is now being appealed to the City Commission. In addition to this, total staff costs total $1,172.55. The Special Magistrate's synopsis setting forth the reason(s) for granting this reduction is included in the backup materials.

attachments.name: 2025-051 RESO PROPOSED OPERATING MILLAGE RATE GENERAL OP FY 2025-2026

description:
This budget proposes an ad valorem operating millage rate of 6.4196, the same rate as the prior year.
The proposed voted debt service millage rate for the 2008 City Hall Bond has decreased from 0.1782 for Fiscal Year 2024-25 to 0.1661 for Fiscal Year 2025-26 (-0.0121 mils, -6.8%) due to the increase in city-wide property taxable values.
The overall city-wide millage rate, combining the operating and debt service rates, will decrease in FY2025-26 by 0.0121 mils, or 0.2%. The FY 2024-25 overall millage rate was 6.5978; the proposed FY2025-26 overall millage rate is 6.5857.
The City's budgeted operating ad valorem revenues for Fiscal Year 2025-26, as adjusted by the expected collection rate (96%), are $15,315,439. This amount is based on the Broward County Property Appraiser's (BCPA's) July 1 certified property taxable values.
For homesteaded property under the Save Our Homes amendment, Florida state statutes limit the increase in assessed value to 3% or the percentage of the change in the Consumer Price Index (CPI) for the preceding calendar year. This year, the Florida Department of Revenue set the maximum increase for homesteaded property at 2.9% for Fiscal Year 2025-26 property tax rates.
Section 200.065(5), Florida Statutes limits the amount a government may increase its millage rate with a simple majority vote of the governing body. A complicated formula is used to calculate this limitation - see Draft Form DR420-MMP in the backup. Due to this restriction, the maximum millage rate the City Commission may approve this year by a majority vote (3 votes) is 6.2506. A two-thirds vote (4 votes) may approve a millage rate up to 6.8757. A unanimous vote is required to approve any millage rate between 6.8757 and the statutory cap of 10.

attachments.name: 2024-013 ORD Amending Fence Walls and Hedges
Fiscal Impact Analysis Fence Regulations 6.10.2025 CC

description:
Section 045-040, “Fences, walls and hedges” of the City’s ULDRs includes regulations for the height, location, and type of fences to be located with the City of Wilton Manors supplemented by Article 030 of the City’s ULDRS for parcels located in the Urban Center Mixed Use Districts. City staff proposes amendments to Section 045-040 of the City’s ULDRs to address issues related to privacy, aesthetics, and safety for properties neighboring parcels that were required to be elevated to comply with Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA) floodplain requirements.
Proposed changes from June 10, 2025 City Commission meeting:
Section 045-040(C)(6) - Clarified previously proposed language to require a fence or wall on a property elevated to comply with Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA) floodplain requirements to be installed at a height of six (6) feet above the highest finished grade.
Section 045-040(C)(7) - Add subsection (7) with language allowing fences with a height of eight (8) feet in rear and side yards adjacent to parcels required to be elevated per Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA) floodplain requirements.
Section 045-040(I) - Revise language to prohibit new chain links on properties within residential zoning or use.

attachments.name: Florida Statues  718.604 to 718.622 Regarding Condo Conversions
Article 30 Condo Conversion and next steps 7.22.2025 CC

description:
Per Section 030-040 of the City's Unified Land Development Regulations (ULDRs) in order to receive additional height, properties are required to meet all eight (8) incentive criteria along with one (1) optional requirement with no exception and which no variances may be granted. One (1) of the eight (8) mandatory additional height incentive criteria is the requirement of an affordable housing component which states, "for projects requesting additional stories, a minimum of two point five (2.5) percent of the total proposed residential units shall be dedicated as affordable housing or payment in lieu of the two point five (2.5) percent dedication in the amount of $50,000.00 per unit for the total number of units dedicated as affordable units. A hotel shall be exempt from the affordable housing component. If a project provides payment in lieu of, the monies shall be deposited into the City of Wilton Manors Affordable Housing Trust Fund. Effective October 1 of each year, the payment in lieu of fee shall be adjusted by the change in the Consumer Price Index (CPI), Miami-Fort Lauderdale-West Palm Beach, all items for December of the previous calendar year. If a project constructs the affordable housing units. the units shall be part of the project and shall remain affordable for a minimum of thirty (30) years from the date of issuance of a Certificate of Occupancy for the project. A declaration of restrictive covenant shall be entered into with the City prior to the issuance of the first building permit. The restrictive covenant shall run with the land and be binding on the developer's heirs, successors, assigns, and transferees. The restrictive covenant is subject to review and approval of the City Commission and, at a minimum, will require an opinion of title or similar evidence of the status of title and encumbrances. In the event an affordable housing component is provided hereunder, no additional payment shall be required under Section 080-090 ULDR".
City staff asks the direction of the City Commission to consider whether a process is required to allow for the payment in lieu for units that were previously dedicated as affordable housing to satisfy the affordable housing component of the additional height incentive criteria per Section 030-040 of the City's ULDRs for the conversion of an approved rental project to a condominium.
title: Article 030: Discussion regarding the change of an approved project utilizing incentives for additional height from a rental to a condominium as it relates to the mandatory affordable housing component criteria.

attachments.name: 2025-048 RESO Approving State Highway Lighting, Maintenance, and Compensation Agreement with FDOT

description:
Powerline Road - SR 845 (NW 9 Avenue), Oakland Park Boulevard - SR 816, and Wilton Drive - SR 811 are owned and operated by the Florida Department of Transportation (FDOT). Pursuant to Florida Statutes, FDOT may enter into agreements with municipalities to perform certain maintenance functions for its roadway facilities and to provide compensation for such maintenance.
The proposed State Lighting, Maintenance, and Compensation agreement updates the current highway lighting maintenance agreements to ensure consistency in language and compensation statewide. It also formalizes the City’s annual compensation based on the number of lighting fixtures located within FDOT rights-of-way.
The City will be responsible for repairing lighting fixture outages within its jurisdiction due to malfunctioning equipment, automobile accidents, etc. Under the agreement, fixed annual compensation is calculated at a per-fixture rate of $347.84 for Fiscal Year 2026, with an automatic increase of 3% (three percent) each subsequent fiscal year.

description:

attachments.name: Minimum Unit Size Presentation 7.8.25 CC Meeting

description:
At the request of the City Commission, City staff has brought forth the topic of minimum floor area of a residential dwelling unit within the Wilton Drive Arts and Entertainment District (WDAE), Transit Oriented Corridor North (TOC-N), Transit Oriented Corridor South (TOC-S), Transit Oriented Corridor East (TOC-E), and Transit Oriented Corridor West (TOC-W) zoning districts also known as the Urban Center Mixed Use Districts for discussion. The zoning regulations for the Urban Center Mixed Use Districts can be found in Article 030 of the City's Unified Land Development Regulations (ULDRs). In Section 030-020 "Definitions", the minimum floor area of a dwelling unit is defined as six hundred (600) square feet, excluding hotel rooms. However, the residential unit must meet the minimum square footage for a dwelling unit or sleeping room per the Florida Building Code, as amended from time to time. In addition, a unit designated and constructed as an affordable housing dwelling unit shall have a minimum floor area of four hundred (400) square feet.
City staff researched the minimum square footage of residential dwelling units for eleven (11) comparable cities within the South Florida area. The minimum square footage ranges from four hundred (400) square feet to twelve hundred (1,200) square feet depending on unit type. A table has been provided with the results of this research as an attachment to this agenda item.
title: Article 30 dwelling unit size

CASE SUMMARY FOR APPEAL 18-794 UDC MANORS LLC

description:
Code Case #18-000794: The owner of the property located at 1550 N.E. 26 Street at the time of the violation, UDC Manors LLC was sent the first Notice of Violation on March 19, 2018, for property maintenance and landscape violations, requesting compliance within thirty (30) days, or the case would be brought to the Special Magistrate. The property was not brought into compliance, and the Special Magistrate Hearing was set for May 2, 2018.
On May 2, 2018, the Special Magistrate heard this case and affirmed the violations, giving the property owner until June 3, 2018 to achieve compliance or face a fine of $50.00 per day plus a $150.00 administrative fee. Routine inspections were completed on this property seeking voluntary compliance with negative results. Failure to achieve compliance within the required time prompted the case to be scheduled for the December 5, 2018, Special Magistrate Hearing to impose the fine and lien on the property.
On December 5, 2018, the Special Magistrate rendered an Order Certifying and Imposing Fine and Lien on the property.
On May 19, 2025, and per Chief Gary Blocker, the code case was administratively complied in the interest of pending development to support lien reduction request proceedings. By that time, the property had remained in violation for a total of 2,541 days minus 155 days for COVID relief (March 9, 2020 thru August 10, 2020) for a total of 2,386 days, resulting in a $119,300.00 lien.
On June 5, 2025, the Special Magistrate denied the request for a lien reduction which is now being appealed to the City Commission. The Special Magistrate's synopsis setting forth the reason(s) for denying this reduction is included in the backup materials. The Special Magistrate also authored an addendum to correct the lien amounts in the associated documents that did not reflect the required COVID relief calculation.
title: Appeal to a lien reduction order by Special Magistrate: Code Case #18-000794 - 1550 NE 26 Street (Police)

description:
On February 27, 2024, the City Commission approved Resolution No. 2024-022, which authorized an agreement for Neucor Construction to construct the NE 24 Street Drainage Improvement Project pursuant to ITB 2024-01. During the course of construction, two conditions became apparent which required the City to issue change orders for the agreement, as well as modification of Purchase Order 24-1413.
Change Order #1 – Modifications to the design depth of pre-cast catch basins due to conflicting unknown existing utilities. The cost of $9,602.65 represents a 4.65% increase in the contract amount.
Change Order #2 – Replacement of an existing driveway section within the public right-of-way to improve stormwater flow. The cost of $1,680.20 represents a 0.81% increase in the contract amount.
The original contract amount of $206,709.42 increased by $11,282.85, resulting in a combined change order total increase of 5.45% over the contract amount. Section 2-58(n)(2) of the City’s Code of Ordinances requires authorization of the City Commission where the sum of all change orders issued under the contract exceeds five (5) percent of the original contract amount.

description:
Planned Unit Developments (PUDs) shall be subject to the development standards specifically established within the PUD document for the given PUD. The standards approved by the City Commission shall govern all use and development of the PUD. Per Section 040 of the City's Unified Land Development Regulations (ULDRs), the development standards include, permitted uses, access, off-street parking and loading requirements, landscaping, traffic, open space, underground utilities, pedestrian and bicycle circulation, energy consumption which includes satisfaction of green building requirements, buffer and compatibility, setbacks, minimum and gross acreage, and height. The final approved site plan will become part of the PUD document.
In accordance with Section 040-130 of the City's ULDRs, the applicant may request exceptions from requirements that are not feasible or applicable to a particular property or proposed development in lieu of requesting a variance from the ULDRs. The applicant has requested five (5) exceptions: 1) from the required number of parking spaces, 2) the dimensional requirements of 79 parking spaces within garages, 3) from the requirement to provide ten (10) foot landscape buffers abutting public right-of-way, 4) from the requirement to provide a five (5) foot landscape buffer abutting side common property line, and 5) from setback requirement where parcels adjoin single family uses or single family districts.
The applications associated with this project were accepted on July 25, 2024, and scheduled for their first Development Review Committee on August 13, 2024. The Development Review Committee reviewed the proposed project based on development standards in effect on and prior to the date of the acceptance of these applications. Ordinance 2024-009 was adopted by the City Commission on September 24, 2024, which amended the regulations of Article 040 – Urban Infill/Redevelopment Planned Unit Development (PUD) District. These amendments include changes to the PUD standards that include, but are not limited to, parking regulations, open space, ultimate distance a building can be from the centerline of a roadway, minimum acreage of the PUD, submittal requirements, and amendment procedures. The applications were reviewed based on the PUD development standards in effect prior to the adoption of Ordinance 2024-009. However, final site plan approval of the proposed project will be determined by the City Commission pursuant to Ordinance 2024-009.

Twelfth Amendment to Baxter  Woodman Term Engineering Agreement - Continuing Contract (RFQ 2020-09) Signed

description:
The Southeast Florida Regional Climate Change Compact develops unified Sea Level Rise projections for South Florida. Their most recent report shows observed average tide levels from 2000 to 2023 have increased by 6 inches, and by 2070 will increase by 21 to 40 inches. As a result, extreme tides and King tide levels during blue-sky conditions are more intense. Weather patterns over the last several years are producing more frequent and intense rainfall events, from passing storms to hurricanes. These events, both individually and in combination, increase Middle River water levels due to storm drainage runoff from its abutting cities and South Florida Water Management District water releases through the C-13 canal to the Intracoastal. High water levels cause river water to back up through the City’s storm drainage outfall pipes and onto roadways. The two main impacts when this occurs are rainfall that cannot drain from roads into the Middle River, and increased roadway flooding during extreme tides.
The City’s implementation of a Tidal Valve Program (Program) as referenced in Section 4.6.2 – Sea Level Rise, of the City’s Water, Wastewater & Stormwater Integrated Master Plan (Plan) will mitigate flooding events. The City’s outfall pipe inventory consists of (88) locations. There are an additional (5) outfalls owned by the State and (6) outfalls owned by Broward County, which are not included in the Program. Ten of the City’s locations will have valves installed during drainage upgrade projects as recommended in the Plan.
The Plan recommends installing inline check valves, which are one-way flow valves installed inside the pipe that allow stormwater to flow out but prevent river water from flowing inward. The Program includes inspecting and assessing outfall structures, prioritizing valve installations, and providing for construction operations. The City’s consultant, Baxter & Woodman, Inc. (B&W) has proposed to provide overall project management, data collection, regulatory notification and approval, contract documentation and bidding services, and construction services for a cost of $73,966.00 per their proposal dated April 17, 2025.

description:
The Wilton Manors Police Department seeks City Commission approval to authorize the disbursement of $1,000 from the Law Enforcement Forfeiture Trust Fund (LEFTF) to Legacy Builders Consulting Group, Inc., in support of the department’s participation in a public service campaign aligned with community engagement and public safety objectives. Legacy Builders submitted a formal funding application requesting $15,000, outlining four sponsorship tiers to support initiatives including the Juneteenth Pride Celebration and the launch of the “All Love No Hate” campaign. Following internal evaluation and consideration of program alignment and available resources, the Chief of Police authorized sponsorship at the $1,000 Legacy Champion level. This funding will support the development and dissemination of a professionally produced public service announcement (PSA), featuring department personnel and promoting messages of safety, cultural diversity, and inclusion.
The Chief of Police certifies that this expenditure meets the criteria set forth under Florida State Statutes, Chapter 932, Section 932.7055. This expenditure also aligns with the objectives of the Law Enforcement Forfeiture Trust Fund (LEFTF) by fostering community trust, enhancing police-community relations, and supporting proactive crime prevention through inclusive outreach.
title: Motion to approve disbursement of Law Enforcement Forfeiture Trust Fund monies as a contribution to Legacy Builders Consulting Group, Inc.

description:
HarmonyWaves, Inc., a nonprofit organization, has submitted a special event permit application to host the Authenticity Music Festival, a weekend-long concert and cultural event that will take place along Wilton Drive. This event builds upon the previous year's Rock the Block and is expected to attract approximately 5,000 attendees.
The road closure will begin at 3:00 AM on Saturday, February 14 and extend through 4:00 AM on Monday, February 16 to allow for event setup, operations, and breakdown. HarmonyWaves will host a live concert series with food, beverage, and vendor booths from 3:00 PM–11:00 PM on Saturday and 12:00 PM–10:00 PM on Sunday.
Per the terms of the permit, HarmonyWaves will be responsible for all direct staffing costs associated with public safety, inspections, permitting, and event support. The City has agreed to provide staff assistance with pre-event planning, site logistics, and committee coordination. All standard special event regulations, including accessibility compliance, ADA access to gated areas, emergency medical services, and use of the City’s WeatherBug Lightning Alert System, will be enforced.
The permit clearly states that sidewalks must remain accessible to the public and outlines requirements for maintaining access behind The Shoppes of Wilton Manors during waste collection operations. HarmonyWaves has also committed to hosting two public meetings in advance of the event and to submitting all required documentation, permits, and proof of insurance within the established deadlines.
General admission to the event is free and open to the public. Donations will be accepted, and VIP areas will require separate ticketing. All marketing materials must clearly reflect these details.
title: Motion to approve Special Event Permit for Authenticity Music Festival (formerly Rock the Block) to be held on Wilton Drive on Saturday, February 14, 2026, and Sunday, February 15, 2026.

P106691 - City of WIlton Manors - Location 2 - CITY Addendum to Lease
P106691 - City of WIlton Manors - Location 2 - Lease

description:
In 2016, the City contracted with EVgo to install one (1) fast-charging EV stall in the City Hall/Hagen Park parking lot. This charging stall, which can accommodate one vehicle at a time, is located near the one-hour parking area facing Wilton Drive—a prime location. The City does not receive any revenue from this stall, and it is common to see two to three vehicles waiting to use it. Three parking spaces were dedicated to install the charging stall.
Under a new lease agreement with EVgo, 10 additional fast-charging EV stalls will be added in an underutilized section of the City Hall/Hagen Park parking lot, near the volleyball court. These new chargers feature updated technology capable of charging vehicles up to seven times faster and will position Wilton Manors as a leader in EV infrastructure in Broward County.
The City will commit 11 parking spaces in the proposed 15-year lease agreement (with an optional 5-year extension). EVgo will pay the City $3,300 per month in Year 1. This amount will increase annually by 3% to adjust for inflation. These chargers will provide a service that is in high demand in our area as well as revenue to the City.

FEC License Agreement- Grade Crossing Matters NE 24 Street MP338+1615

description:
The Broward Metropolitan Planning Organization (BMPO) is the recipient of a federal grant pursuant to the Railroad Crossing Elimination Program (RCEP Grant), which will help fund the Broward County Sealed Corridor Project. This project aims to improve safety in Broward County, Florida, by installing enhancements at 21 grade crossings along the Florida East Coast Rail Corridor, owned by FECR. The Corridor is used by FECR, to operate freight rail, and Brightline, which provides intercity passenger rail service.
City of Wilton Manors has one crossing located at NE 24th Street that is included in this project.
RCEP grant will fund the design and construction of the project through an agreement with the BMPO. Brightline will complete the work pursuant to a sub-recipient agreement with the BMPO. The County and each of the municipalities have also entered into a Grant Participation and Reimbursement Agreement for the Implementation of the RCEP Grant. The City of Wilton Manors has an existing crossing agreement with FECR for the NE 24th Street crossing dated 9/26/2002. In order for Brightline to construct the improvements on behalf of the cities, they are requesting the attached agreement, authorizing Brightline to be the third party beneficiary to the City's agreement with FECR.

attachments.name: 2025-034 RESO Approving OnSolve Order Form for CodeRed Subscription

description:
Congruent with the City's Strategic Plan Priority Area of Proactive Public Safety, the CodeRED emergency system allows pre-authorized City staff to disseminate information to residents and visitors during active emergency situations via a 24-hour a day, 7-day a week cloud-based notification network. Notification is made to both landline and cellular telephones by either a pre-recorded message or text communication. During an active emergency situation, landline and cellular telephones within the geographic boundaries of the City can be instantly notified of active threats to life and property. Additionally, CodeRED users from other municipalities and states would receive notifications of emergency situations if they are physically present in the City or are approaching the City's geographic boundaries. Other functionalities of the CodeRED system allow residents and visitors to elect to receive non-emergency information updates such as road closures, water main breaks, and details regarding City events.
The service contract provides for an annual option to renew the contract. The current renewal is for 1/25/25 to 1/24/26. The cumulative cost for our contract with OnSolve for CodeRED has exceeded the $30,000 threshold requiring Commission approval. As such, we are seeking approval to renew the contract.

P106691 - City of WIlton Manors - Location 2 - CITY Addendum to Lease
P106691 - City of WIlton Manors - Location 2 - Lease

description:
In 2016, the City contracted with EVgo to install one (1) fast-charging EV stall in the City Hall/Hagen Park parking lot. This charging stall, which can accommodate one vehicle at a time, is located near the one-hour parking area facing Wilton Drive—a prime location. The City does not receive any revenue from this stall, and it is common to see two to three vehicles waiting to use it. Three parking spaces were dedicated to install the charging stall.
Under a new lease agreement with EVgo, 10 additional fast-charging EV stalls will be added in an underutilized section of the City Hall/Hagen Park parking lot, near the volleyball court. These new chargers feature updated technology capable of charging vehicles up to seven times faster and will position Wilton Manors as a leader in EV infrastructure in Broward County.
The City will commit 11 parking spaces in the proposed 15-year lease agreement (with an optional 5-year extension). EVgo will pay the City $3,300 per month in Year 1. This amount will increase annually by 3% to adjust for inflation. These chargers will provide a service that is in high demand in our area as well as revenue to the City.
